His spirit remains as the North Wind over Wolvendom; in 6.4 the part of him left in Nod-Krai, corrupted, also chose to return its power to the ley lines.

65.content:
Heavenly Principles (also: Phanes, Primordial One, First Descender, Great Ruler of the Firmament, First Usurper, Pitkamoonen, Lord of the Seven Calamities): The Heavenly Principles is the god who rules Teyvat from Celestia: the First Descender, a being from the sea of stars beyond the false sky. It conquered the dragon Sovereigns, remade the world, created humanity, and governs through "laws" enforced by its four Shades, the Archons' thrones and the Gnoses. Before Sun and Moon calls it the Primordial One and suggests the name Phanes. It has slept since the Cataclysm 500 years ago, but Celestia still acts in its name.

Ordinary people know only a distant heaven. Dragons and rebels call it a tyrant or usurper, and the Tsaritsa's Fatui, the Abyss Order and the Traveler's sibling all work toward opposing it.

Established: It made four Shades, copies of itself: Naberius (Life), Ronova (Death), Istaroth (Time), Asmoday (Space). It took the Sovereigns' Authorities, which became the Archons' Authorities, and it enclosed Teyvat under the false sky. About 6,000 years ago it defeated the dragon king Nibelung in the War of Funerary Flame but was badly wounded.

Celestial nails punish lands that defy or test its order. It distrusts forbidden knowledge, the Abyss and beings who seek power beyond their station. It edits the world's records through Irminsul. Descenders stand outside its laws, and Irminsul does not record them.

Nature: It is said to be winged, crowned and androgynous, of "gender unknowable". It is absolutist: it loves humanity on its own terms and strikes hard at threats to its order.

History: It conquered the dragons, rebuilt the world and created humans, who lived in a unified civilisation under the heavens. After winning the War of Funerary Flame it cast down the celestial nails and set up the Gnoses and seven thrones. It slept after the Cataclysm.

Before Sun and Moon dates the conquest to forty years and the creation of life and humans, with the Shade Naberius, to four hundred years after it. Humans made a covenant with it, and their one taboo was temptation. In the war it shattered the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and flung the Frost Moon beyond the sky. Its nails devastated Sal Vindagnyr, Hyperborea and Lang-Gan, and it banned the history before the war.

Saarelainens bargain: Revealed in 7.1: the Heavenly Principles erased Anastasya's existence for opening a gate to the Abyss. The Third Descender, Saarelainen, then traded his body to become the seven Gnoses. In return it restored her and promised never to harm his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns. Its price was that it wiped him from all memory through Irminsul. He bound the promise with a curse that would strike if it was broken, and Anastasya concludes that this curse is why it has slept since the Cataclysm.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 it is still asleep. Celestia's monitoring cycle keeps watching Teyvat and the Shades, and in 7.1 it reclaimed Ronova's Authority of Death.

The Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses and is preparing to face it. The Traveler's sibling says it will certainly wake.

Connections: Its seat is Celestia. The Four Shades are its parts, and The Seven sit on its thrones. Its works include the Gnoses, Visions (through the Archon system), the false sky, a refashioned Irminsul, the nails and fate. Its foes are Nibelung, the Abyss, Khaenri'ah, the Tsaritsa, the Abyss Order and Apep.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation): keep it offstage. It is asleep, has no present-day voice, and has never been shown speaking. Show it through Celestia's directives, the Shades, the nails and people's reluctance to name it. Commoners know "Celestia" and "the gods", not this history.

Portrayal notes (common mistakes to avoid): - The "unknown god" who separated the twins is Asmoday, "Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles", not the Heavenly Principles itself.
- "The Second Who Came" in Before Sun and Moon means Nibelung.
- It is not an Archon, and it is dormant, not dead. Do not give it a fixed gender, a face or dialogue.

66.comment: Heavenly Principles: Before Sun and Moon on the Primordial One
66.content: Before Sun and Moon, a banned history in The Byakuyakoku Collection, is the fullest in-world account of the Primordial One. When the "eternal throne of the heavens" came, it fought the seven dragon-lords and made four shining Shades of itself. After forty years the Sovereigns fell and the nations submitted. Four hundred years after "the Held Branches", it and one Shade created animals, plants and humans, who made a covenant with it and entered a new age. The author suggests the Primordial One "may have been Phanes", a winged, crowned, androgynous being born from an egg, who used the eggshell to separate the universe from the "microcosm of the world".

67.comment: Heavenly Principles: Saarelainen's curse on the Heavenly Principles
67.content: Saarelainen's curse was the safeguard on his bargain with the Heavenly Principles: it would strike if the promise to spare his descendants, the Khaenri'ahns, was broken. Anastasya concluded in 7.1 that the Cataclysm in Khaenri'ah triggered it, and that this is why the Heavenly Principles sleeps. His body became the seven Gnoses, and the Heavenly Principles erased all memory of him through Irminsul.

68.content:
Holy Soil (also: Holy Soil phenomenon, hallowing of soil, Holy Soil of primordial ice): Holy Soil is land that holds a high concentration of the primordial elemental power of the three realms. Dragons can thrive in it; humans cannot live or farm on it. The process of land becoming Holy Soil is called the Holy Soil phenomenon. Canon shows it on Watatsumi Island, in ancient Natlan and across ancient Snezhnaya, and at the end of Version 7.1 Ronova tries to give it to the whole world.

The term is used by different speakers for different places, so a character should say which land they mean. It is a lore term, not a gameplay status or zone.

Established: - Watatsumi: local folklore says the island's spirit hears the call of Enkanomiya and sinks toward its depths. The Sangonomiya Shrine sends someone to Enkanomiya every few centuries to fetch a Bloodbranch Coral left by Orobashi to seal the vishaps, then performs the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri to make the sunken spirit return.
- What the ritual really does (Tsumi, in the limited-time Three Realms Gateway Offering event): it awakens Orobashi's second familiars, the Sangacorallia, creatures that break the Light Realm's primitive elemental energy down into the milder energy of the Human Realm.
- During the limited-time Three Realms Gateway Offering event (Version 2.5) the ritual did not reverse the phenomenon but only stopped it, which Kokomi says had never happened before. Investigation showed the Void Realm had invaded Enkanomiya and suppressed interaction between the Light Realm and the Human Realm. The matter was resolved, but the source of the Bloodbranch Coral was cut off when the vishaps rescued their sealed kin.
- Natlan: the speaker the wiki identifies as Kukulkan says that, in an earlier eon, the Heavenly Principles regarded the phlogiston-rich soil that sustained Natlan as Holy Soil and cast sky-nails down to destroy the land. Dragons, being adaptable, were forced to devolve to survive in the new Natlan and became the saurians, though their bloodline did not change.
- Snezhnaya: Aksinya, citing record fragments from the Shadow Realm, says that when Hyperborea tried to make the Primordial Human from the Cryo Dragon Sovereign's corpse, the experiment ran out of control, and the corpse's unchecked authority turned the whole of Snezhnaya into the Holy Soil of primordial ice. Ley lines there became veins of pure crystal. The Heavenly Principles then sent a nail down on Hyperborea, which sank into the Shadow Realm.

Accounts: - Folklore: Enkanomiya's depths draw away Watatsumi's spirit, bleaching the soil.
- Tsuyuko (a shrine maiden who attended the Sumeru Akademiya): seawater leaches nutrients; Orobashi's Jade Coral Branch replenishes the missing elements and holds off the bleaching.
- Eboshi: the soil is the vishaps' habitat growing, a sign that primordial power is strengthening.
- Kokomi: the Matsuri is meant to reverse the process; during the limited-time 2.5 event it only paused it, and once she learned how the Bloodbranch Coral works she said she may need to think of a new way to counteract the phenomenon.

Open questions: Canon does not say what Holy Soil is at a physical level, or whether the nails cure or merely suppress it.

It is unresolved whether the Holy Soil Ronova meant to release in 7.1 is actually spreading, whether it helps or harms living dragons and vishaps, and what it would do to farmland.

Connections: The three realms and the Light Realm supply the power. Celestial nails and the Heavenly Principles are the response in Natlan and Snezhnaya. Dragons, vishaps and saurians are the beings tied to it. Watatsumi Island, the Sangonomiya Shrine, Enkanomiya, Hyperborea, the Cryo Dragon, the Eitr and Ronova are the places and figures involved.

69.comment: Holy Soil: Holy Soil on Watatsumi Island
69.content: Watatsumi's soil is bleaching and losing nutrients. In The Moon-Bathed Deep, Tsuyuko explains that a Jade Coral Branch left by the Omikami must be retrieved from Enkanomiya for the shrine's ritual (called the Watatsumi Mitama Omatsuri in that quest). Tsuyuko privately attributes the bleaching to seawater leaching nutrients from the soil.

70.comment: Holy Soil: Holy Soil and the Three Realms Gateway Offering
70.content: During the limited-time Three Realms Gateway Offering event (Version 2.5), Kokomi's Bloodbranch Coral ritual only paused the Holy Soil phenomenon instead of reversing it, which she says had never happened before. Tsumi explains that the ritual really awakens the Sangacorallia, which convert raw primordial energy into the milder energy of the Human Realm, and that darkness from the Void Realm was stalling them. The problem was resolved, but the coral supply ended, and Kokomi says she may need a new way to counteract the phenomenon.

71.comment: Holy Soil: Holy Soil in Natlan and Snezhnaya
71.content: Kukulkan says a nail was cast on phlogiston-rich Natlan and forced the dragons there to devolve into saurians. Aksinya says the Cryo Dragon's corpse turned Snezhnaya into the Holy Soil of primordial ice until a nail struck Hyperborea. At the end of 7.1 Ronova breaks the Snezhnaya nail with the Eitr, meaning to give the world the feeling of death and the hallowing of soil.

72.content:
Iridescent Moon (also: Sonnet's moon, moon of Sonnet): The Iridescent Moon was the third and smallest of the Three Moons, raised by the Dragon King Nibelung and governed by Sonnet, the youngest of the Three Moon Sisters. Its light was the faintest of the three, barely visible to the naked eye, but it produced fleeting halos when it shone. The Heavenly Principles shattered it in the war of funerary flame. Sonnet, in agony over her broken moon, fused her fading soul with the Abyss to stay alive, and the Iridescent Moon became the baleful Crimson Moon. Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty later worshipped it as a source of Abyssal power. Its husk and Abyss-corrupted Moon Marrow were hidden in an otherworldly domain, which the Traveler and Columbina entered in the Nod-Krai Archon Quest (6.1).

Established: - Smallest and last-made of the Three Moons; its goddess was Sonnet.
- Faint light, fleeting halos.
- Shattered, then fused with the Abyss as the Crimson Moon.

- Nibelung made the moons with Secret Source technology and raised them from the planet's crust at what is now Nod-Krai.
- Sonnet shared sovereignty of the night sky with her sisters, one at a time, riding in a silver carriage. The English text says they switched about three times a month; the Chinese uses the looser unit xun.
- When the moon fell, the sisters' carriage was overturned and the palace of the stars ransacked, according to the Liyue book Moonlit Bamboo Forest.

History: Nibelung left, the sisters kept Teyvat for him, and then the Heavenly Principles arrived and were received as guests. After Nibelung returned and imprisoned the sisters, the Heavenly Principles shattered the moon. Sonnet fused the remains with the Abyss.

Sonnet was horrified at the Heavenly Principles' treatment of anyone who challenged them, and thought it excessive for the offences. After the Heavenly Principles overthrew the Seven Sovereigns, the sisters entered a precarious peace with them, which the dragons saw as betrayal. When Nibelung returned from the Abyss, the sisters disagreed about whether to take sides. He took it for disloyalty, sealed them in the moon's reflection and made their moons into weapons. The Heavenly Principles shattered the Iridescent and Eternal Moons and threw the Frost Moon beyond the false sky.

Sonnet stayed imprisoned in the reflection after her moon was shattered, ignorant of the war. In True Moon (6.3) a future Columbina reached her, and the truth shocked her. Of the three sisters she feared death most and looked to the others for comfort as the prison began to wear down her body. The sisters gave Columbina the authority of all three moons and asked to be sent back to Teyvat, mortal, where history records they died.

Present day: As of 7.1 the Iridescent Moon is a broken husk in a sealed Abyssal domain, Sonnet is dead, and its Marrow is held by Arlecchino. The shadowmoon illusion is gone and only the Frost Moon, returned under the false sky, lights the night.

Accounts: - Liyue books say the sisters died fighting each other, or that only two died and the moon in the sky is one of their corpses. Treat these as folk memory.
- Dragon-side accounts treat the sisters as traitors to Nibelung.

Open questions: - Who or what sealed the Marrow in the Abyssal domain, and when.
- What the dark presence in the domain was. Canon does not say.

Connections: Sonnet (its goddess); Nibelung (creator); the Heavenly Principles (destroyers); the Abyss (what it fused with); the Crimson Moon, the Crimson Moon Dynasty and Khaenri'ah; Arlecchino and the Balemoon Bloodfire; Columbina, Dottore and the Traveler; the Frost Moon and the Eternal Moon (siblings).

73.content: The Iridescent Moon Marrow was sealed in the Crimson Moon's domain, corrupted by the Abyss. The Traveler cleansed it (6.1) and Columbina gave it to Arlecchino. Dottore stole it, and after his defeat Columbina returned it to her again.

74.content:
Irminsul (also: World Tree, Sarva, Irminsul tree, Irminsul trees, silver-white tree): Irminsul is the primordial silver-white world tree of Teyvat. It grows downward in a vast cavern deep underground, and the Ley Lines are its roots. Through them it gathered the world's memories into one repository. The Dendro Archon's consciousness is bound to it, and outsiders such as the Traveler have no records in it. In Version 6.6, after Dottore hijacked and corrupted it, Nahida burned Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis, and Aaru took over its role.

Irminsul is older than the Heavenly Principles. They took it over and remade it into a recorder of all information and an anchor for the world's fate.

Established: Tighnari (3.0) says the Dendro Archon is called the God of Wisdom because of this link, and that her power is said to be a manifestation of Irminsul.

Silver-white trees with glowing blue streaks, known as "withered trees", Petrified Trees or Irminsul trees, are parts of Irminsul across Teyvat. Domains, Ley Line Outcrops and Ley Line Blossoms belong to the same network. A mind can connect to Irminsul: the Dendro Archon does so by nature, and the Traveler briefly did in Chronic Illness. Fate is written into the tree; Nahida says the Fontaine prophecy was "carved into Irminsul long ago".

Origins: Apep (6.6) says the Heavenly Principles did not plant Irminsul. It existed in the age of the dragons, looked and worked very differently, and its Ley Lines carried the power of the Light Realm. The Heavenly Principles took it over, made it serve humanity and used it to anchor fate.

Memory and erasure: Purging information from Irminsul takes power on the level of a god. A purge rewrites everything recorded about its subject, including memories, books and letters. The events and their consequences remain, but people remember different causes or different actors. Natives of Teyvat never notice the change, Archons and Paimon included. Only beings with no records, such as the Traveler, keep the original memories.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, Irminsul is destroyed; only its underground parts remain. Aaru, King Deshret's unfinished afterlife, was rebuilt to collect and store the world's information in its place.

Nahida says the fire burned for seven days and nights, and most of Teyvat's vital information was saved. Nicole moved Nahida's connection to Aaru, so the loss did her no harm. With Irminsul burned, Nahida says, fate "now carries many more possibilities." The Pyro Gnosis vanished in the fire.

Connections: Ley Lines (its roots), Nahida, Aaru (its successor), the Heavenly Principles and fate.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): after 6.6, Irminsul is gone and Aaru holds the world's memory. Natives must not remember erased people or events, such as Greater Lord Rukkhadevata or Scaramouche's original history; only the Traveler, other outsiders and those whose records were restored know the old versions.

75.content: In Version 6.6 (Song of the Welkin Moon, Acts IX and X), Nahida fell into a coma, chaos spread through Sumeru from the Ley Lines, and finally a giant Irminsul tree rose in Sumeru City. Dottore had entered Irminsul through death, a route Nahida could have closed only by cutting every soul off from the Ley Lines. Once he was inside, her authority was quickly restricted, and Pantalone had placed Dottore's last backup in the Ley Lines. Sumeru's defenders overloaded Irminsul with the Akasha to stop its growth. Wanderer and the Traveler went inside while the world's information was moved into Aaru. Nahida invoked her "supreme authority as the keeper of Irminsul" and lit the Pyro Gnosis, which Mavuika had given her. Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius consented, and the flames burned the tree and Dottore with it.

76.comment: Irminsul: Aaru as the new Irminsul
76.content: King Deshret built Aaru with illicit celestial technology as an unfinished afterlife, and it once held three of his Seven Pillars prisoner. In 6.6 Sumeru's scholars reprogrammed it, and during the battle the world's information was moved into it out of Irminsul. Aaru now collects and stores what the Ley Lines carry. Nahida calls it the new Irminsul, and her own existence is now bound to it.

77.content: Known erasures: the Third Descender Saarelainen, erased by the Heavenly Principles long ago (revealed 7.1); Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, removed by Nahida in 3.2; Scaramouche's past, erased by himself in 3.3; and forbidden knowledge, erased by Nahida and the Traveler. Each time, natives' memories and records were rewritten while the consequences remained. Memory of Saarelainen survived only with the Belyi Tsar, who was hiding in the Shadow Realm at the time, and in Celestia's own records, which Rhinedottir says she has read.

78.content: Silver-white trees with glowing blue streaks stand across Teyvat as parts or root-ends of Irminsul: on Dragonspine (the Frostbearing Tree, plus one on a small island further east), in The Chasm, on Tsurumi Island near the "Boatman", and in the Orchard of Pairidaeza on Mt. Damavand. Ley Line disorders warp the land around them. The wiki notes that they stand where Celestial Nails are thought to have struck. The Dragon-Queller, the Sacred Sakura and the Weeping Willow of the Lake have similar streaks but brown bark, and are not counted as Irminsul trees.

79.content:
Irminsul Modifications (also: Irminsul purge, Irminsul erasure, erased from Irminsul, purged from Irminsul, history rewriting): Irminsul, the silver-white tree that stores Teyvat's information, can be edited. A god-level power can purge a person or fact from it, and memories, books and records across Teyvat then change to match, while the events themselves still happened and their results remain. Three purges are known: the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata (by Nahida, 3.2), Scaramouche (by himself, 3.3) and the Third Descender Saarelainen (by the Heavenly Principles, revealed 7.1). In 6.6 Dottore hijacked Irminsul and Nahida had it burned down.

The edits touch people's memories and physical records (books, letters, item and character texts), but not the underlying events, so rainforests Rukkhadevata grew, or crimes Scaramouche committed, remain and are simply remembered with other causes or actors. People native to Teyvat, including gods, do not notice they were altered. Descenders and other outlanders have no records in Irminsul and so keep their memories.

Established: Irminsul collects the world's information through the Ley Lines and acts as the record of Teyvat, so removing something there removes it from the shared understanding of the world. Rewriting changes whatever counts as Teyvat's information: what people remember and what books and letters say. Natives, including the Archons, do not notice. Paimon is affected too, while the Traveler is not. Removal appears to happen only once: information that natives of Teyvat preserve or retrieve afterward does not disappear again, though retrieval is presumably hard without the help of someone who never lost it, such as the Traveler.

Accounts: Rukkhadevata: In Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies Nahida removes the Greater Lord, whose existence had been contaminated by forbidden knowledge and kept polluting Irminsul after her death. Afterward Nahida believes she was always the original Dendro Archon who lost her memories fighting the darkness in the cataclysm. The other Archons and the people of Sumeru remember only Lesser Lord Kusanali (in the voice-overs of Venti, Zhongli and Ei, "Buer"), and the Akademiya's reasons for confining Nahida change to disappointment in her weakness.

Scaramouche: In The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call (Interlude Chapter, Inversion of Genesis) Scaramouche erased his own past from Irminsul. He could not erase himself entirely and continued to exist as the Wanderer, but he lost the memory of his earlier identities. Records elsewhere were rewritten: Ei and Yae Miko lose their Kunikuzushi voice-overs and Tartaglia his Balladeer voice-over, Fatui NPC lines are changed, and Inazuma's account of Tatarasuna and the fall of the Raiden Gokaden is retold without him.

Saarelainen: In the 7.1 Archon Quest (Black Feathers Scattered at Parting) Rhinedottir, who says she read Celestia's records of the incident, tells Anastasya that Anastasya was first erased by the Heavenly Principles as punishment after the Belyi Tsar incited her and Saarelainen to open the gate to the Abyss. Saarelainen then ascended to Celestia to bargain for her return, offering his own life. The Heavenly Principles agreed on condition that everything about him be forgotten: they erased him and all related memories from Anastasya's mind and used Irminsul to erase every trace of the Third Descender from the world.

Open questions: Canon does not explain how the purge power works in detail, why self-purging fails, how much else the Heavenly Principles have edited without anyone noticing, or why the Traveler's sibling has records in Irminsul while the Traveler has none.

Connections: Irminsul, the Heavenly Principles, the Ley Lines, the Akasha System and Aaru, Descenders, Fate, the Shades, and the destruction of Irminsul in 6.6 are the neighbouring entries. Characters most affected are Nahida, the Wanderer, Dottore, the Belyi Tsar and the Traveler.

80.content: Nahida removed the Greater Lord Rukkhadevata from Irminsul in Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies to cleanse the pollution of forbidden knowledge. Gods, mortals and Nahida herself now remember only Lesser Lord Kusanali, who believes she lost her memories in the cataclysm. The forests she grew and Sumeru's traditions remain.

81.content: Scaramouche tried to remove himself from Irminsul in the Interlude Chapter and succeeded in erasing nearly all records of his past, but he could not remove himself and lives on as the Wanderer, no longer recalling his earlier identities. Before this, Nahida had prepared a memory block that would remind him of his past regardless of changes to Irminsul, and gave it to him after the Traveler recognised his new identity as Wanderer.

82.content: According to Rhinedottir in the 7.1 Archon Quest, Saarelainen ascended to Celestia and traded his own life to have Anastasya restored; the Heavenly Principles' condition was that everything about him be forgotten, and they used Irminsul to erase every trace of him. Memories of him were wiped and records altered, but traces remain.

83.content: After the Doctor's Nod-Krai half was destroyed, part of his Omega Build stored in Northland Bank infiltrated Irminsul and overrode Nahida's authority for a time. It produced red mist that drove people mad, unusual Ley Line blossoms, and a giant Irminsul tree in Sumeru City that Nahida described as a sign of unchecked greed.

84.content: Nahida, within Irminsul, invoked her right as its keeper and faced the Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius, who asked whether she was certain she wished to use her authority to destroy Irminsul, the tree through which the Heavenly Principles maintain fate. She said humanity's survival came before Irminsul. They allowed it, and the Pyro Gnosis burned the tree; the Doctor died, dragged into the flames by the Segments he had deleted. Aaru took over Irminsul's role and Nicole's reliance on Irminsul was transplanted there.

85.comment: Irminsul Modifications: Additions and Records of Outlanders
85.content: Additions are rarer. Nahida arranged for Dottore's recorded memory of killing Niwa Hisahide to be preserved and findable when Scaramouche searched for Descender records, and admitted to the Wanderer in As Though Morning Dew that she planned this deliberately. Beings not from Teyvat, such as Descenders, do not normally appear in Irminsul, but the Traveler's sibling has records there, which characters link to Khaenri'ah.

86.content:
Kuuvahki (also: blessing of the Moon Goddess, polar kuuvahki): Kuuvahki is a moon-power found only in Nod-Krai: a pure, primordial form of elemental energy belonging to the Light Realm, comparable to phlogiston. It flows through Nod-Krai's air, land, plants and animals. The Frostmoon Scions call it "the blessing of the Moon Goddess"; Snezhnograd researchers named it "kuuvahki." It powers Moon Wheels, Lunar Reactions and Nod-Krai machines.

Ineffa also compares it to the Primordial Sea. The Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest (6.3) reveals that kuuvahki is the body of Columbina, the Moon Goddess, poured out over Nod-Krai about 6,000 years ago.

Established: - It is linked to the Three Moons and is strongest when the Frost Moon comes closest to Teyvat. Many creatures grow stronger or weaker with its tides.
- Kuuvahki strong enough can counter the Abyss and even turn Abyssal power into something usable.

- It has two opposite polarities, red and blue: like colours repel, opposite colours attract. Where it is very strong, "the rules by which objects move and operate" change.
- It drives Aino's "Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Energy Cannon" over Nasha Town, which fires when the Wild Hunt threat gets too high, and the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle, a source of new technology and weapons.
- Radiant Beasts are ordinary animals warped over ages by kuuvahki into stronger, element-attuned creatures. Some plants store kuuvahki.

Accounts: Before the truth came out, locals explained kuuvahki either as the power of the moons that Nibelung raised from Nod-Krai, or as the remains of two shattered moons whose fragments fell on Nod-Krai.

Origin: In The First Sliver of Moonlight (6.3), Columbina, fleeing Dottore through the "moon's reflection", travels back to the War of Funerary Flame and meets the Moon Sisters Aria, Canon and Sonnet. They tell her kuuvahki did not exist in their time: it is simply her power. Made Trilune Goddess by their authorities, she turns her body into moonlight poured over Nod-Krai alone, and that moonlight becomes kuuvahki. It answers her because it is her.

Moon wheels and reactions: Moon Wheels, the Vision-like gems of Ineffa, Lauma, Flins and others, channel kuuvahki instead of ordinary elemental energy. Lunar Reactions also harness kuuvahki.

The Lunar Reactions are Lunar-Charged, Lunar-Bloom and Lunar-Crystallize. Zibai of Liyue is the only known Moon Wheel user from outside Nod-Krai; Istaroth gave her hers.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): kuuvahki is Nod-Krai's main exploration mechanic. Kuuvahki plants, red or blue kuuhenki and similar sources give a red or blue "empowered state" for lifting, throwing and smashing objects, disabling Fatui machines and riding Moonlanes.

Open questions: - How kuuvahki relates to ordinary elemental energy, and how Zibai's Moon Wheel works outside Nod-Krai, are not explained.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): in Nod-Krai kuuvahki is part of the landscape. Plants glow or lean toward passers-by, animals are livelier or more sluggish with its tides, and red or blue glows suit polarity effects.

87.content:
Ley Line Disorder (also: Ley Line Disorders, Ley Line Disturbance): Ley Line Disorder is the in-game term for the odd conditions inside Domains and some Spiral Abyss chambers. Depending on the place, the surroundings may hurt or hinder fighters (falling icicles, lightning, a creeping cold, drained energy) or boost them (stronger reactions, higher damage). It sits on the border between game rule and setting: Domains are said to stand on Ley Lines, but canon never explains each effect as a story event.

Treat it mainly as a gameplay label with an in-world flavour: Domains are built on the Ley Lines, and energy surging through the Petrified Tree at a Domain's heart is how the Ley Lines entry accounts for such effects. The same word is also used for a few Trounce Domains that replay old battles as "Memories".

Established: - The wiki defines Ley Line Disorders as effects inside the Spiral Abyss and certain Domains that help or hinder characters, separate from enemy auras and elemental nodes. It has existed since 1.0.
- Domains are tied to the Ley Lines: item and loading text say Domains stand on Ley Lines around Petrified Trees (see the Ley Lines entry).

- Hazards and debuffs seen in Domains include Sheer Cold (a temperature bar that drains HP), periodic lightning bolts that drain Energy, falling icicles, longer Frozen duration, unstable High-Energy Crystal Cores dropped by defeated foes, a spreading Plasma Field, a pursuing Chaos Cluster, enemy Attendants that bolster a leader, and alternating Energy Tides.
- Four elemental debuffs exist: Smoldering Flames (Pyro damage over time), Slowing Water (longer skill cooldowns), Engulfing Storm (draining Energy), and Condensed Ice (higher Stamina use). Each lasts while the matching element stays on the character and can be cleansed by applying a self-aura of an element that dispels it.
- Beneficial Disorders include raised elemental damage, boosted reactions (Overloaded, Electro-Charged, Swirl, Superconduct), HP-threshold bonuses, CRIT damage, Plunging Attack, melee and ranged buffs, Shield and Elemental Mastery buffs, and shockwaves that trigger on certain actions.

Accounts: - Game text: the Ley Lines entry records loading-screen lines saying some characters are "recognised" by disturbed Ley Lines and boosted in Disorder Domains, and that those touching disturbed Ley Lines may be carried to hidden Domains where foes from their memories appear. That is a rule-of-play description, not a witnessed event.
- Story quests: separate Ley Line disturbances (Abyss Order tampering in 3.5, corruption in Sumeru in 6.6) are narrated as real events in the Ley Lines entry. None of them names a "Ley Line Disorder" in the Domain sense.

Open questions: - Whether the hazards in Domains are natural properties of the Ley Lines beneath them, a product of their builders, or only a gameplay abstraction.
- Whether "Memories" Domains are the Ley Lines replaying recorded events; their descriptions suggest it, but canon does not state a mechanism.

Connections: Ley Lines, Irminsul and its Petrified Trees, Domains, the Spiral Abyss, elemental reactions and auras.

Ley Line Blossoms and Outcrops are the open-world counterpart. Disorder effects draw on the elements and reactions, so they connect to the element and reaction entries.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): in Domains and Abyss chambers, Disorders are the environmental rule set for the challenge. A Domain can show one or several, and values differ by Domain and difficulty. Elemental debuffs apply to each party member independently (Smoldering Flames affects only the active character), pulse on a fixed interval, and are shortened by artifacts and elemental resonance when the Domain applies them. Some self-applied auras can cleanse them.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): characters can describe a Domain's strange cold, lightning or surging energy as the Ley Lines acting up beneath it. Most travellers would treat it as a known hazard of Domains, not a mystery. Do not have a character explain its cause as settled fact; canon does not.

88.content:
Ley Line (also: Ley Lines, leyline, leylines, Earth Veins): The Ley Lines are a hidden network that links all of Teyvat. Elemental energy flows through them, and they carry the memories of everything that happens in the world, from the surface to the deepest depths. They were tied to Irminsul, the world tree, which stored what they gathered. Disturbed Ley Lines can make people see memories that are not their own.

Ley Lines existed in the age of the dragons, but the Heavenly Principles refashioned them, along with Irminsul, into a defence for the world against the Abyss and an anchor for fate. Natlan is the great exception: its own Ley Lines were destroyed in an ancient war, and the Night Kingdom serves in their place.

Established: - Elemental energy flows through the Ley Lines, and loading-screen lore says they "remember all things" that happen in the world.
- Tighnari compares them to the roots of Irminsul. They reach up to the surface from a vast cavern deep underground, and they keep absorbing the world's memories and funnelling them into the tree.
- Where the flow of energy is blocked, deposits form at the surface and Ley Line Blossoms bloom. All Domains are said to be built on Ley Lines, around silver-white Petrified Trees that are parts of the Irminsul root system.

- Original Resin item text says the roots of all the Irminsul trees and blossoms intertwine at the deepest, most hidden place in the earth, and that the pattern they make defines the Ley Lines. Condensed Resin text says these trees are connected to Ley Lines that have become blocked over time, and that resin energy can purify the blockage.
- Disturbances carry memories. In the Interlude act Caribert (3.5), the Abyss Order tampered with the Ley Lines near Avidya Forest, and the Traveler fell unconscious and saw their sibling's memories from centuries before. Dainsleif later observed that Abyss Order activity is usually followed by Ley Line trouble.
- The Ley Lines are linked to erosion. The Raiden Shogun says that as long as they flow, the relentless erosion of time will never stop (Farewell to the Past, 2.5).

Origins: Before the Heavenly Principles arrived, the Ley Lines and Irminsul already existed. According to Apep (6.6), the Ley Lines then carried an abundant, primitive form of elemental energy: the power of the Light Realm. The Heavenly Principles usurped and refashioned Irminsul, made it serve humanity and used it to anchor the fate of the world. The Light Realm's power was diluted into the elemental energy of the human world.

Accounts: - Mavuika (5.3): the forces of the Abyss always seek to corrode Teyvat; the Ley Lines were created by the Heavenly Principles, and only their protection lets Teyvat nurture life.
- Apep (6.6) and Kukulkan (5.5): the Heavenly Principles took an existing network and converted it, rather than making it from nothing.

Natlan and the night kingdom: Natlan lacks stable Ley Lines of the ordinary kind. Mavuika (5.1) says its Ley Lines took the worst damage in the ancient war between the Descender and the dragons, which let the Abyss in. Guided by Ronova, the angel Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, rebuilt a similar network from the fragments: the Night Kingdom, which functions as Natlan's Ley Lines.

Open questions: - Whether the Ley Lines and Irminsul's roots are literally the same structure, or two linked systems.
- Why the Traveler and Descenders are not recorded.

Connections: Irminsul (the memory store), the Heavenly Principles (who refashioned the network), the Abyss (which it protects against), Domains and Ley Line Blossoms (surface outlets) and Ley Line Disorders (unstable energy in Domains).

Erosion and fate both flow through this network. Natlan's Night Kingdom is a stand-in network, and Aaru is the repository since 6.6.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not literal lore): Ley Line Outcrops are open-world challenges. Defeating the enemies reveals a Ley Line Blossom (a Blossom of Revelation for character EXP materials, or of Wealth for Mora), claimed with Original Resin. Domains and their Petrified Trees and Ley Line Disorder effects are tied to the Ley Lines in the same way.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Ley Lines as an unseen, underground current. Most people only know them through Domains, blossoms, scholars' talk or strange memories and ghosts. A disturbance can plausibly cause dizziness, disorientation, odd elemental behaviour or flashes of another person's memory.

89.content: The Loom of Fate is a Khaenri'ahn device made by Caribert and the Abyss Order that can weave Ley Lines. In its incomplete form it could only create and implant memories. According to Caribert (Bedtime Story, 4.7), once complete it gains the power to weave real Ley Lines and loses its lesser power over memories. He also said new Ley Lines can neither replace nor extend Teyvat's existing ones.

90.comment: Ley Line: Ley Line Blossoms and Petrified Trees
90.content: Ley Line Blossoms grow from deposits where the flow of elemental energy is impeded, at the ends of the Ley Lines. They are said to take root in people's wills: a "Revelation" blossom answers a desire for battle, a "Wealth" blossom a desire for money. Petrified Trees, silver-white extensions of Irminsul, stand at the heart of Domains and channel the Ley Lines; the surge of energy through them causes Ley Line Disorders. Both can be revitalised with resin.

91.content:
Light Realm (also: realm of the elements, Vishap Realm): The Light Realm, also called the realm of the elements or the Vishap Realm, is one of Teyvat's three realms. It is the home and origin of pure, primordial elemental beings, above all dragons and elemental lifeforms, and the raw source from which the seven elements were later drawn. It stands directly opposed to the Void Realm (the Abyss) and is not naturally compatible with the Human Realm.

Canon treats it as the elemental energy of the world before it was divided, like white light before it is split into seven colours. Its energy vanquishes the Void Realm's darkness. Modern Elemental Energy is a narrowed, more easily controlled and human-compatible form of it.

Established: - The Light Realm hosts creatures that wield pure, raw elements. Dragons and elemental lifeforms are its best-known inhabitants.
- It is diametrically opposed to the Void Realm and incompatible with the Human Realm unless adjustments are made.

- Its dragons were ruled by the Seven Sovereigns under the Dragon King Nibelung, who were later succeeded in rulership by the Three Moons.
- When the Heavenly Principles arrived, it and its shades defeated the Seven Sovereigns, founded the Human Realm and narrowed and refracted the Light Realm into the seven elements (per the banned book "Before Sun and Moon").
- It then used phlogiston as inspiration to modify the Light Realm's power into modern Elemental Energy, easier for humans to control and better suited to fight the Abyss (Beneath the Secret Source, as relayed by the wiki).
- The Human Realm was at some point interposed between the Light and Void Realms (The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent).
- Realm-crossing adaptations exist: vishaps were modified to accept Orobashi's Bloodbranch Coral, Sangacorallia break the Light Realm's pure elemental energy into something the Human Realm can bear, and Natlan's Holy Soil was similarly rendered tolerable with Grainfruit and the Essence of Sacrifice. The Void Realm, by contrast, is incompatible with both and dangerous to both.

Accounts: - The banned book "Before Sun and Moon" presents the Heavenly Principles' refraction as founding the Human Realm. The Pale Crown Palace noble's notes present the same narrowing as a loss: boundless possibility confined in the name of certainty. Both are in-world views; canon does not name one the whole truth.

Event accounts: - During the limited-time 2.4 event Three Realms Gateway Offering, Tsumi, the Snake-Masked Shrine Maiden, describes the three realms' analogous currents (ley lines for the Human Realm, elemental currents for the Light Realm, dark currents for the Void Realm) and says the Light Realm's energy vanquishes the Void Realm's darkness.

Open questions: Canon does not say what the Light Realm physically is, where it lies, or how its currents work. The three realms appear to be concurrent facets of the world rather than separate places, with some areas dominated by one realm's power.

Connections: Three realms: cosmology.three-realms. Abyss (Void Realm): cosmology.abyss. Rulers and inhabitants: Seven Sovereigns, Nibelung, dragons, vishaps, elemental lifeforms. Refraction into elements: Heavenly Principles, system.elements, system.phlogiston. Regional forms: kuuvahki and the Three Moons in Nod-Krai (see also Archaeolune Energy on the Frost Moon), phlogiston in Natlan. Enkanomiya: Enjou's trick and the Three Realms Gateway Offering.

How {{char}} behaves: This section is the project's suggested narrative handling, not canon. Most characters will not know the term "Light Realm"; scholars, dragons, vishaps and those close to the Heavenly Principles or Fatui research might. Keep it mysterious, and do not state fan theories as fact.

92.content: The Light Realm (realm of the elements, Vishap Realm) is the primordial source of pure elemental energy and the home of dragons and elemental beings. Opposed to the Void Realm and incompatible with the Human Realm without adaptation. The Heavenly Principles defeated its Seven Sovereigns and narrowed it into the seven elements.

93.content: Teyvat's three realms are the Light Realm, the Void Realm and the Human Realm made by the Heavenly Principles. They appear to coexist as facets of the same world rather than separate places. The Light Realm's energy overcomes the Void Realm's darkness. The Void Realm threatens both others.

94.content:
Moon Envoys (also: Moon Envoy, Lunar Envoy, Lunar Envoys, Envoy of the Lunar Palace, envoys of the moon): Moon Envoys were servants of the Three Moons who lived in the Lunar Palace during the era of the unified civilization. The name is a title, not a species: an angel or someone who was not one could hold it. Known examples are Zibai, Thoth and, by inference, Nabu Malikata. After the war of funerary flame killed the moon goddesses, the office lost its purpose.

The envoys carried out many divine duties. Some laboured across the moons to guide humanity and weave the threads of fate for living things, while others came down to the mortal realm to bless nations with good harvests. They could take animal forms and travelled by lunar chariot.

Established: - After the Three Moons accepted the Heavenly Principles' divine plan, the new masters sent subordinates to share the sisters' work, and Moon Envoys were assigned to assist each goddess. In a remembered scene, Sonnet says the work can simply be left to the Moon Envoys.
- Envoys lived in the Lunar Palace above the clouds.
- Souls of the dead once followed the Moon Envoys' trail to the cities on the moons, where they rested.

- The title could be held by any individual, angel or not. Zibai, an angel who guided Lang-Gan, became an envoy when Istaroth, the Ruler of Time, gave her a crest bearing the sigil of the moons; her character story says she never fully accepted it. The crest is her Moon Wheel.
- Duties varied. The furnishing text for the Moon Envoy of Silver Radiance says some envoys toil across the three moons to guide ignorant mortals, others descend to bless a nation with bountiful harvests, and that the title does not name one specific person.
- Envoys could change shape into animal forms and used a lunar chariot to travel, for example between the Lunar Palace and Lang-Gan, according to the wiki's summary of Zibai's quests.
- The Lunar Palace is also called the Moon Capital; boatmen such as Diotima and Euthyphro ferried souls toward it, and Diotima says the souls followed the envoys' trail.

Open questions: - Whether boatmen and Moon Envoys were one role or two.
- Which moon each named envoy served; only Zibai's link to Sonnet is argued, and from indirect evidence.
- Whether Nabu Malikata and the Mistress of Chenyu Vale were envoys; both are inferences.

Connections: Three Moons and their goddesses Aria, Canon and Sonnet; the Heavenly Principles and angels; the unified civilization; the war of funerary flame; the shadowmoon that hid the moons' fate; Istaroth; Zibai, Thoth, Nabu Malikata; the Moon Wheel; Lang-Gan; the afterlife systems of the moons and, later, the ley lines and Irminsul.

95.comment: Moon Envoys: Zibai as a Moon Envoy
95.content: Zibai was an angel who guided the nation of Lang-Gan and was later made a Moon Envoy when Istaroth gave her a crest of the moons. In the wiki's reading she was assigned to Sonnet of the Iridescent Moon, who left much of her work to her. She travelled between Lang-Gan and the Lunar Palace by lunar chariot. She died defying the Heavenly Principles over the Celestial Nail, and was restored in the Lantern Rite event story (6.3). Her own entry carries the detail.

96.comment: Moon Envoys: Thoth the Moon Envoy
96.content: Thoth, the Ibis King and Lord of Lies, is described as a former Moon Envoy of the Lunar Palace and a colleague of Zibai. He later served King Deshret as a Seven Pillar. His claim of laboring across the three moons to guide mortals comes from Nefer's recollection of him, and she doubted it, but other texts back the envoy role.

97.content:
Moon Marrow (also: Moon Marrows, Eternal Moon Marrow, Iridescent Moon Marrow, Artificial Moon Marrow, Marrow of the Eternal Moon, Marrow of the Iridescent Moon): A Moon Marrow is a divine artifact: an energy core formed from a Moon Goddess's remains after her death. Moonchanters in Nod-Krai long sensed a divine presence in the Eternal one and named it the Marrow. It exists in three forms: the Eternal Moon Marrow (Aria), the Iridescent Moon Marrow (Sonnet, corrupted by the Abyss) and an Artificial Marrow that Fatui Harbinger Dottore made himself. Columbina compares the Marrow to an Archon's Gnosis, and it can only form once a goddess is dead.

Established: - Formed from the remains of a dead Moon Goddess; it holds her power and divine imprint.
- Eternal Moon Marrow: from Aria, a miniature moon ringed with debris. Sealed away by the Frostmoon Scions and able to show past events.
- Iridescent Moon Marrow: from Sonnet, a red crescent wreathed in crimson flame when uncorrupted. Corrupted by the Abyss.
- Artificial Marrow: made by Dottore, a light-blue mechanical sphere with esoteric patterns.

- Columbina, the living Frost Moon goddess, says a Marrow can only form after the goddess is dead, so she does not carry one herself. She compares it to a Gnosis, which was formed from the body of the Third Descender; a god who bears a Gnosis is an Archon.
- A Marrow is a source of primordial Light Realm energy that predates the Heavenly Principles.
- Each Marrow belongs to its own goddess. Columbina says the three moons are not one and the same and that, as the Frost Moon goddess, she cannot wield the others' powers. She also says one body cannot contain the Marrows of two moons.
- A goddess can still restore her own strength by drawing kuuvahki from a Marrow. Columbina does this with the Eternal Marrow, saying moonlight blends and each moon can reflect the others' glow.
- Dottore's Artificial Marrow counted as a genuine article for completing the Trilune.

Accounts: Eternal Moon Marrow: it coalesced from Aria's remains and was found and kept as a sacred relic by the Frostmoon Scions. They sealed it in a secret chamber that opens only once a year, on Moon-Prayer Night, when the moon is nearest Teyvat and kuuvahki in Nod-Krai peaks. Its power can reveal past events, especially when a Moon Goddess wields it.

Present day: As of the end of the Song of the Welkin Moon finale (6.3), the Eternal Moon Marrow is in Lauma's keeping, in the Frostmoon Scions' secret chamber. The Iridescent Moon Marrow, purified of its corruption, is held by Arlecchino. The Artificial Marrow was destroyed with Dottore's defeat. This section follows the wiki's account; later 6.x or 7.x events that moved the Marrows were not found.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat a Marrow as a sacred relic, not a trinket. Nod-Krai residents and the Scions regard the Eternal one with reverence. Only characters who were present for the Song of the Welkin Moon should know the details of Sonnet's purification, Dottore's artificial Marrow or Columbina's role.

98.content: The remains of Aria, goddess of the Eternal Moon, condensed into a miniature moon ringed with debris. The Frostmoon Scions kept it as a sacred relic in a chamber that opens once a year, on Moon-Prayer Night. It can show past events, especially in a goddess's hands. Lauma stored it in the Traveler for a time, and after Dottore's defeat she restored it to the chamber.

99.content: Sonnet's Marrow, a red crescent in flames when uncorrupted. Abyssal energy twisted it into the Balemoon Bloodfire and the Crimson Moon Dynasty hid it in a domain opened only by a Bloodfire ritual. The Traveler freed and purified it during the 6.1 story, and Arlecchino now holds it.

100.content: Dottore's creation, a light-blue mechanical sphere with esoteric patterns, built in the False Moon Institute. It stood in for Columbina's strength after she banished herself and let him control the Trilune power. It was destroyed when he was defeated.

101.content:
Ode of Resurrection (also: Rite of Resurrection, Rite of Rekindling): The Ode of Resurrection is the ceremony, held at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in Natlan, that revives warriors bearing an Ancient Name who have died fighting the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars. An officiator recites a eulogy, the Pyro Archon walks into the Sacred Flame to find the fallen and their Name in the Night Kingdom, and the crowd sings until the Archon steps out again with the revived. It only works if the warrior's team won. It is the reason Natlan could send its best into endless war.

It is also called the Rite of Resurrection, and Mavuika's character stories call it the Rite of Rekindling. It heals only the fatal wound, not injuries gathered earlier in the battle or existing illness. After the Abyss was defeated in 5.3 the ceremony was discontinued.

Established: - Who qualifies: only Ancient Name bearers. For that reason warriors without a Name were not sent to the Night Warden Wars.
- Condition: at least one member of the fallen warrior's team must return victorious. If an entire team falls, none can be restored.
- Where: at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, through the Sacred Flame, a conduit to the Night Kingdom.

- Those not brought back are stranded in the Night Kingdom, and their Ancient Names are eventually forgotten and lost. Natlan's saying is that the victors burn bright while the losers turn to ash.
- The healing applies only to fatal injuries. It does not mend wounds accumulated during a long battle or pre-existing ailments (Mavuika's character story).
- Warriors who are never lost to the Night Kingdom eventually retire from age or injury, die normally, and their Ancient Name passes to another warrior, so the Names carry Natlan's history across generations.
- Natlanese who die otherwise enter the Night Kingdom, slowly lose their sense of self in the sea of souls, and are in time reborn in Natlan in other forms. The Ode is the exception for bearers who fell in victorious battle.

Ceremony: An officiator opens with a eulogy addressed to the warriors of Natlan, calling on them to heed the call of life as inheritors of memory and legend and naming Natlan's fire as the nation's lifeblood. The Pyro Archon then steps into the Sacred Flame to seek the dead and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom. Meanwhile the crowd in the stadium bows its head and sings in Swahili.

The song's refrain is that the tale continues on: glory passes through generations, courage lights sky and earth, victory will again herald Natlan's path, and the living will wait and sing until the heroes come back and burn bright once more. The melody and lyrics are an excerpt of the Natlan soundtrack, sung in Swahili. At the end the Archon emerges from the flame with the resurrected person. Mualani describes this as the usual sequence before Kachina's Ode, and later recalls Kachina humming the song during training breaks.

History: Natlan's tradition holds that the Ode was made possible when Xbalanque borrowed power from Ronova. Through the Pilgrimage the strongest Ancient Name bearers were chosen and sent to fight the Abyss in the Night Warden Wars, and the Ode let them fight knowing they could be brought back.

Connections: Sacred Flame and Night Kingdom (the ceremony's means and destination), Night Warden Wars and Pilgrimage (the system it supports), Ancient Name (who may be revived), Mavuika (the Archon who performs it), Kachina (its failure and the final use).

102.comment: Ode of Resurrection: Ode of Resurrection
102.content: The Ode of Resurrection is Natlan's rite for reviving Ancient Name bearers who fell fighting the Abyss, provided at least one of their team returned victorious. At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame an officiator speaks a eulogy, the Pyro Archon walks into the flame to find the fallen and their Name in the Night Kingdom, and the crowd sings that the tale continues on. It heals only the fatal wound. Its power was borrowed from Ronova, Ruler of Death, by Xbalanque.

103.comment: Ode of Resurrection: Kachina's Failed Ode
103.content: Kachina's Ode was led by Mavuika with Ntotila as officiator. Mavuika returned from the Sacred Flame alone, saying neither Kachina nor her Name could be found. Some in the crowd, led by Tepexpan and Tamuin, doubted Kachina's worth; Mavuika declared her a hero. She suspended the Pilgrimage and began investigating. She later said the Abyss's unrest in the Night Kingdom had blocked her.

104.comment: Ode of Resurrection: Ronova and the Borrowed Power
104.content: Quest text says the Ode's power comes from Ronova, the Ruler of Death, who let Xbalanque borrow it. In 5.3 Ronova required the Archon's life as the price for the power used in the war. The Lord of the Night held back the blow, and Capitano merged his life force with the Lord of the Night instead.

105.content:
Primordial Human (also: Narayana, Proto-Man, Primordial Humans, Ruler of Elysium, King of Elysium, Svarod, Velikan of Light): The Primordial Human, also called Narayana, is a title: the ruler of Teyvat in "the court of the stars". Nibelung, the dragon king, held it before the Heavenly Principles destroyed him, and the seat has been vacant since. Later efforts tried to create a new bearer: the Hyperboreans' project that produced the Belyi Tsar, the Frostmoon Scions' Sacred Heir Project, and Rhinedottir's Primordial Human Project, which produced Albedo.

In 7.0 the Pale Crown Palace quest line shows Aksinya's attempt to complete the Belyi Tsar's ascension to the title at the cost of the world as it is. The term also appears in a Nicole voice-over, where in another possibility Albedo was the "Primordial Human" who traveled through worlds "recording and creating all".

Established: - Narayana is another name for the title (Aksinya, 7.0). An artifact text speaks of a "vacant seat in the court of the stars", which the wiki identifies with it.
- Nibelung, called "the One" by Aksinya, is tied to the seat; after his destruction it has sat empty.
- Hyperborea tried to produce a new bearer from the remains of the Cryo Dragon. The result, born about a thousand years after the experiment, was the Belyi Tsar, the first Cryo Archon.

- Because Nibelung was still alive when Hyperborea ran its experiment, notes in the Pale Crown Palace say the seat was still occupied and the experiment could not reach its goal.
- The experiment ran out of control. The Cryo Dragon's unchecked authority turned the land into the Holy Soil of primordial ice, and the Heavenly Principles dropped a nail on it, which sank Hyperborea into the Shadow Realm.
- Aksinya says the Belyi Tsar knew he was the failed product of that project, yet accepted it, and with the Hvergelmir institute set out to become the true Primordial Human. The Eye of Graeae was the "Proto-Man" built to complete this.
- In the world quest An Ark That Used to Be a Soul (7.0) the Traveler stops Aksinya's plan to open the Court of Bliss, in which the Tsar would ascend and a "Courtyard of Carefree Light" would replace the world.

Accounts: - **Aksinya (7.0):** the seat of Primordial Human, or Narayana, has been empty since Nibelung's destruction, and the Belyi Tsar was meant to fill it.
- **Artifact text (Disenchantment in Deep Shadow):** the Snow-King, burdened by sin and remorse, assembled the Hvergelmir to seek the stairway to the vacant seat in the court of the stars.
- **Nicole (voice-over, About Albedo):** in another converged possibility, Albedo was the "Primordial Human" who traveled through worlds, "recording and creating all". She adds that once that journey ended, no one could guarantee whether he would choose destruction or salvation. The wiki generalises this into a description of Primordial Humans.

Open questions: - Whether the office has any holder now. No canon says it does.
- Whether Nibelung's title and Narayana's seat in "the court of the stars" are the same idea as being a Descender.

106.comment: Primordial Human: Nibelung and the vacant seat
106.content: Aksinya calls Nibelung "the One": a will born alongside Teyvat, master of the Light Realm's power in the beginning and king of the Dragon Lords. She says the place of Primordial Human, or Narayana, has been vacant since his destruction. The wiki, citing the same quest, lists "Primordial Human" among his titles. His rank as Second Descender rests on the war of funerary flame, covered in the Descenders entry.

107.comment: Primordial Human: Hyperborea's project and the Belyi Tsar
107.content: Hyperborea tried to forge a new Primordial Human from the flesh and blood of the Cryo Dragon. The experiment went out of control and the land became the Holy Soil of primordial ice; the Heavenly Principles dropped a nail on the region, and Hyperborea sank into the Shadow Realm. A thousand years later the Belyi Tsar awoke from the remains. Unaware of what he was, he led the Snowland Fae, later learned his origin and, as Cryo Archon, chose to pursue the goal set for him.

108.comment: Primordial Human: The Eye of Graeae as Proto-Man
108.content: Aksinya describes the Eye of Graeae as the "Proto-Man" created through countless experiments, the key that would let the Belyi Tsar become the Primordial Human; its face was modelled on the Tsar's human form. It is the quest NPC Paimon calls Goggles, found by the Traveler in an abandoned train in Chapter VII (7.0). Before the final fight it asked the Traveler what they would do if their sibling had become a different person; the Traveler answered that they would learn to love them again.

109.comment: Primordial Human: The Sacred Heir Project and Avrelian
109.content: The Frostmoon Scions, Hyperborean survivors, ran a Sacred Heir Project instead of the Seed of Life Project: breeding to purify moon-blessed blood until a Maiden bore a being able to wield the Light Realm's energy at will. The prophesied child was called the Ruler or King of Elysium. The wiki lists Avrelian, the first Reed Miller, as the failed outcome: his mother fled the role, and he became a legendary thief and founder of the Treasure Hoarders, executed 500 years ago.

110.comment: Primordial Human: Rhinedottir's Primordial Human Project
110.content: Rhinedottir's Primordial Human Project aimed to create a human through alchemy. It first produced failures such as Subject Two, who took Albedo's form and was discarded in Durin's stomach, and finally the "perfect" Albedo, whom she classed as Cretaceus. Nicole says that in another converged possibility Albedo was the Primordial Human who traveled through worlds.

111.content:
Primordial Sea (also: Primordial Seawater, Water from the Primordial Sea, Primordial Water, primordial ocean): The Primordial Sea is an ancient sea hidden beneath Fontaine. Most life in Teyvat first arose in it, and it once lay on the surface of the world. Its water gives life, and it can also take it away: the people of Fontaine were made from Oceanids using its water, so pure Primordial Seawater dissolved them back into water. This was the root of Fontaine's "original sin" and of the prophecy that a rising flood would dissolve every Fontainian. In the 4.2 Archon Quest, Neuvillette, restored as the Hydro Sovereign, made Fontainians true humans. The flood came, but it no longer dissolved them.

The main known entrance lies beneath the Fortress of Meropide, behind a sluice gate in its Forbidden Zone. Smaller passages and pools exist in other underground places, such as beneath the Tower of Ipsissimus and in an underwater Sinthe production base. People from other nations are not dissolved by it; it only makes them more sensitive to Hydro.

Established: - Pure Primordial Seawater dissolves a Fontainian of Egeria's era or later into water, and their memories merge into the sea. Non-Fontainians are not dissolved.
- Diluted water does not dissolve people but still harms them. Exposed Fontainians show flushed skin, hyperventilation and exhaustion.
- Since Neuvillette's absolution (4.2), Fontainians are no longer dissolved by it.

- Water from the sea is described as having "higher quality and density" than ordinary seawater, and it can be weakened by mixing or dilution.
- In the 4.0 Archon Quest, Neuvillette says the Primordial Sea no longer exists on Teyvat's surface.
- Ordinary people cannot normally enter the sea; Childe reached its depths only after following a voice out of Meropide.
- Sigewinne can diagnose Primordial Seawater exposure from its symptoms (she did so for Freminet, and later testified about Furina).

History: Before the Archons, the sea's "heart" was the first Hydro Dragon, one of the Seven Sovereigns. After the Heavenly Principles removed it, the Hydro Archon Egeria became the sea's new heart. Egeria used the sea's water to give her Oceanids human bodies. The Heavenly Principles judged this a sin, and the Fontaine prophecy followed.

Egeria's people became the tribes of Fontaine. In her reign, repentant exiles were sent below the waves to guard her secret, the entrance to the sea. They built the first Fortress of Meropide over it, and later wardens added gauges to monitor the water level. In time most of the prison's inmates forgot what the gate was for. The Remurian god-king Remus received a goblet of water from Egeria at the sea and used it to build Remuria (see the Ichor entry).

Accounts: - Hydro Vishaps (glider text, which itself calls them unreliable): the first sea was like blood, and life within it was not separate individuals. Creatures that moved onto land or into the sky grew blood vessels to carry the sea inside them, and the first Hydro Dragon was its beating heart.
- Oceanid tales (same text): when that heart was removed, Celestia's envoy, the leader charged with creating life, came to the sea and made another heart, Egeria. She had a dragon's nobility without its form and a god's majesty without a divine duty, and her compassion led her into the sins that beings of pure water must beware.
- Remurian legend (Dross of Pure Sacred Dewdrop): the dense primordial sea is the purest origin of all things and will one day swallow all life; whatever did not arise from it will be filtered out as floating detritus.

Open questions: - Who, if anyone, now acts as the sea's "heart"? Canon says only that Neuvillette, fully restored, could command it.
- Is the Amrita Pool, Egeria's body in Sumeru, made of the same water? The question is unresolved.

Connections: Prophecy of Fontaine (the flood it caused); Egeria, Focalors and Furina (the Hydro Archon's role); Neuvillette and the Hydro Dragon (the sea's original sovereign); Oceanids and the tribes of Fontaine (the people it shaped); the Fortress of Meropide (built to guard its entrance); Remuria (built on water refined from it).

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): after 4.2 the sea is no longer a danger to Fontainians, so a modern scene should not show Fontainians dissolving. Primordial Water can still be shown as a rare, illicit substance tied to Vacher's remnant gang. Before 4.2 it is lethal to Fontainians and almost unknown to the public; most people learned of its power only from Marcel's trial.

112.comment: Primordial Sea: Primordial Seawater and Sinthe
112.content: Water from the Primordial Sea dissolves Fontainians whose bodies came from it. Diluted, it does not dissolve them. Vacher (Marcel) found that weakened water made Sinthe, an addictive drink that brings euphoria. He sold it through dealers in Poisson to fund his research. Long use leaves people unable to focus or control their emotions, and withdrawal brings paranoia, anxiety and severe fatigue. Callas banned it in Poisson. Vacher also used the water to dissolve a man after a shooting, leaving Callas to be blamed. Callas kept silent to protect his daughter Navia, and later died in a duel with Clorinde.

113.content: Deep in the Fortress of Meropide's Forbidden Zone, a sluice gate seals the largest known passage from the Primordial Sea to the surface. Only the warden and trusted people knew of it. Wriothesley worked out that its gauges measured Primordial Water, and that the prison existed to stop the sea from engulfing Fontaine. When the gate burst in 4.1, Neuvillette pushed the water back and resealed it.

114.comment: Primordial Sea: Original sin of Fontaine
114.content: Egeria's Oceanids longed to live as humans, so she poured Primordial Seawater into their "blood vessels" as a substitute for blood, giving them human bodies. Creating human life was beyond her authority, and the Heavenly Principles branded her and her people with an original sin. The decree followed: the waters would rise, every Fontainian would dissolve, and only the Archon would remain, weeping on her throne. Neuvillette's absolution in 4.2 replaced that substitute blood with real blood.

115.content:
Realm of Consciousness (also: realms of consciousness, consciousness realm, space of consciousness): A realm of consciousness is an abstract space built on a person's mind. It lies outside the world of Teyvat, yet what happens inside it can change the outside world. Its entrance takes a shape tied to its owner, and its interior is coloured by the owner's memories. The Traveler visits three: Makoto's (Inazuma), Lesser Lord Kusanali's and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's (Sumeru). Canon says very little about how they work.

A realm can outlast its owner's body: the owner keeps a sense of self after death, but cannot perceive the outside world or the passage of time, and the realm cannot be preserved forever. Yae Miko calls the whole idea "very abstract" and surrounded by chaos.

Established: - It is a domain built on one person's consciousness, separate from Teyvat.
- Events inside can affect the real world.
- The entrance takes a form related to its owner: a torii gate for Makoto, a newly sprouted tree branch for Kusanali, a Knowledge Capsule for Rukkhadevata.
- Its interior is shaped by the owner's memories.

- A realm can exist after the owner's body dies, and the owner can keep their sense of self; but the owner cannot sense the outside world or time passing, and the realm cannot be kept indefinitely.
- Someone else may seal or open the entrance: Ei sealed Makoto's, and the Shogun later unlocked it; Kusanali opened Rukkhadevata's with the Electro Gnosis.
- A realm can be closed from within by a living owner: Kusanali shut hers to keep Il Dottore from reaching her mind through the Akasha.

Accounts: - Yae Miko (Radiant Sakura) gives the only general description: a very abstract concept, surrounded by chaos.
- Kusanali treated Rukkhadevata's realm as a preserved image of Irminsul as it was five hundred years earlier; this is her belief at the time, stated in the quest.

Open questions: Canon does not explain the mechanics of realms of consciousness, who can make one, or what happens to a realm once its owner's consciousness is gone. It does not say whether Focalors' and Furina's spaces in The Opera of Noirceur and Blancheur are realms of consciousness; they merely resemble them in how time behaves. Do not state either as fact.

Connections: Related to Ei's Plane of Euthymia (a mind-world she placed in the blade Musou Isshin), to the Sacred Sakura and Inazuma's cataclysm cleansing, to Irminsul and forbidden knowledge in Sumeru, and to the Akasha system that Dottore used against Kusanali. Adepti personal abodes (sub-space creation) are a separate technique.

How {{char}} behaves: Use as a narrative device, clearly dreamlike and personal: the entrance looks like something the owner would make, the inside echoes their memories, and time outside need not match time inside. Keep explanations vague, as in canon. (This is the archive's suggested use, not a canon rule.)

116.comment: Realm of Consciousness: Makoto's realm of consciousness
116.content: After Makoto died in the cataclysm, Ei preserved her realm of consciousness; its entrance is a torii gate. Ei sealed it, but the Shogun unlocked it when their wills opposed each other so they could fight at full strength, Ei having no body of her own. Makoto had prepared the realm so that Ei could eventually grasp her vision of Eternity, after which Makoto's remaining consciousness in Musou Isshin would give Ei the seed of the Sacred Sakura. Ei planted it in the realm, where it took root in Inazuma's past and absorbed the filth of the cataclysm. Makoto's strength and consciousness were then spent and the realm vanished. The Dream Sakura it yielded remains, visible but intangible.

117.comment: Realm of Consciousness: Kusanali's realm of consciousness
117.content: While Lesser Lord Kusanali was imprisoned in the Sanctuary of Surasthana, she closed off her consciousness so Il Dottore could not read her mind through the Akasha. As part of the plan to free her, the Traveler entered her realm of consciousness; the entrance appeared as a newly sprouted tree branch (quest Jnagarbha Day, Archon Quest Chapter III Act V).

118.comment: Realm of Consciousness: Rukkhadevata's realm of consciousness
118.content: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata's realm was left behind when she died in the cataclysm. Its entrance was a Knowledge Capsule, opened when Kusanali used the Electro Gnosis, which also shielded her somewhat from the forbidden knowledge that had corrupted Rukkhadevata's remaining consciousness. Because Rukkhadevata had been contaminated and was bound to Irminsul, Irminsul could not heal while her memory lasted. Kusanali erased Rukkhadevata's existence and remaining consciousness; the realm, which Kusanali took to be Irminsul as of five hundred years earlier, disappeared. Irminsul was healed and things caused by its contamination, such as Eleazar, vanished (quest Where the Boat of Consciousness Lies, version 3.2).

119.content:
Sacred Flame (also: K'ahk', Natlan's Sacred Flame): The Sacred Flame is the fire that never stops burning above the arena of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Natlan's central landmark. It is the conduit to the Night Kingdom, the realm of the dead and of the Wayob, and the means of speaking with the Wayob. Mavuika calls it the foundation of Natlan's resistance against the Abyss. Battles between Natlanese warriors produce Contending Fire, which fuels it. The Pyro Archon steps into it during the Ode of Resurrection to bring fallen heroes back.

Its main outlet, the column of fire above the arena, can be seen from far outside the Stadium. A second outlet is the large fire pit in the Speaker's Chamber, where the tribal chiefs meet under the Archon's eye. Mavuika put her life into the flame at the end of the Cataclysm 500 years ago and returned from it in the present day.

Established: - The flame is a continuous fire at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and a conduit to the Night Kingdom and the Wayob.
- Contending Fire, produced only in combat between people of Natlan, keeps it burning. Cival explains that Natlan is safe from the Abyss only while the flame burns eternal.
- The Pyro Archon performs the Ode of Resurrection through it.

- When a new Pyro Archon ascends the divine throne, their "inner flame" awakens, and the Sacred Flame grants them broad knowledge and memory of Natlan. Mavuika says this is how she knows the history of Natlan's rules (Echoes of Life, 5.0). In a scene from Mavuika's past shown in A Fuel Named "Fate" (5.1), her friend Wanjiru repeats the idea and worries that inheriting the flame's knowledge can change a person's personality.
- Objects carried into battle by Natlanese heroes slowly become imbued with Contending Fire. Burning them releases that fire as fuel, though crudely and all at once.
- Mavuika says that no one but her could sustain the flame, and that it "must never go out": it frightens the Abyss and is "the pillar of Natlan's stability".

Ode: In the Ode of Resurrection, an officiator recites a eulogy, the Pyro Archon walks into the flame to seek the fallen warrior and their Ancient Name in the Night Kingdom, and the crowd bows and sings until the Archon walks back out with the revived warrior.

Only Ancient Name bearers who fell in the Night Warden Wars qualify, and only if their unit "achieved victory", meaning at least one member came back victorious. The rite reverses only the fatal wound; injuries built up earlier in the battle and existing illnesses remain. Mavuika's character stories call the return a "Rite of Rekindling", treated like a victory feast. As a child she watched her father come back through the flame alive but so badly wounded he could not stand.

History: Mavuika was Pyro Archon during the Cataclysm. After the war against the Abyss she placed her remaining life inside the Sacred Flame so that she could reawaken 500 years later and oversee her plan to drive the Abyss out of Natlan. She woke some years before the Traveler arrived and won the Pilgrimage to become Archon again.

In the Natlan Archon Quest (5.0), the Ode for Kachina failed: Mavuika came out of the flame alone, unable to find her or her Ancient Name, because the Abyss had invaded the Night Kingdom and blocked communication between the flame and the Wayob. Mavuika suspended the Pilgrimage, even though fewer battles meant less Contending Fire. Since Contending Fire alone was "far from sufficient", she then transferred her own power into the flame to keep it alight, giving up, among other things, the ability to turn her hair to flame. To reach Kachina and the Traveler in the Night Kingdom, she burned the keepsakes of past heroes stored in the Speaker's Chamber, using their Contending Fire to open the boundary between the worlds.

Connections: The Night Kingdom, which stands in for Ley Lines in Natlan, lies on the other side of the flame. The flame is not itself a Ley Line.

120.content: Contending Fire is the energy produced when people of Natlan fight one another, and the fuel of the Sacred Flame. The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame existed largely to generate it, which is why outlanders were barred: their participation would hinder its production. Items carried in battle by heroes absorb some of it over time. Mavuika burned such keepsakes in 5.0 to force open the way into the Night Kingdom, and their power was spent in an instant.

121.comment: Sacred Flame: Mavuika's sleep in the Sacred Flame
121.content: After the Cataclysm, Natlan was ruined and its tribes broken. The Archon and the tribal heroes agreed on a 500-year plan to rebuild the tribes until each Wayob could choose a new hero. Because Natlan had no gods able to extend a human life, Mavuika placed her life in the Sacred Flame, dying before her time so that she could wake again when the plan matured. She revealed this in Past and Future (5.0).

122.content:
Sea of Stars (also: the universe beyond Teyvat): The Sea of Stars is the universe beyond Teyvat: thousands of planets, stars and civilisations lying past the false sky and the Dark Sea. Canon describes it as a dangerous "black forest". The Heavenly Principles, Saarelainen and the Traveler all came from it, and unknown threats and cosmic calamities such as Surtalogi, the All-Devouring Narwhal and the Abyss reside there. Teyvat is one planet among them.

Most Teyvatians cannot see it at all, because the false sky hides the cosmos from the planet. It is not an accessible location in the game and appears in animated shorts, weapon and book text and character stories.

Established: - Teyvat's planet sits on the edge of a spiral arm of an unnamed galaxy in the sea of stars.
- Three of the four Descenders came from beyond Teyvat (the wiki counts the Heavenly Principles as the first Descender, Saarelainen as the third and the Traveler as the fourth). The Abyss is counted among the cosmic calamities that reside there.
- Unknown cosmic calamities live there too.

- In the Old World, Nibelung made the Eternal, Frost and Iridescent Moons from the planet's crust to govern it while he travelled the sea of stars. During his absence the Heavenly Principles descended on Teyvat, took control and raised the false sky, which kept the universe hidden.
- During the Funerary Year Nibelung returned, brought the Abyss to the world and fought the Heavenly Principles, who won and still rule Teyvat. The Eternal and Iridescent Moons were shattered, and the Frost Moon was thrown out beyond the false sky into the sea of stars. By the Archon Quest "True Moon" it had been revitalised and drawn back inside the false sky.
