- After the Cataclysm, Surtalogi brought Skirk to Teyvat from her homeworld, and gave the weakened All-Devouring Narwhal to Skofnungr in the Primordial Sea.

Worlds: Known worlds beyond Teyvat. Teyvat itself. The Traveler's unnamed planet, which the Traveler and their sibling once ruled before a "star-devouring darkness" destroyed it; they then began travelling between worlds in a spaceship. Skirk's unnamed planet, home to humans who can adapt to any environment or energy source; a merchant ship from a neighbouring world judged them a potential threat and an army attacked, and Skirk escaped with Surtalogi's help. Throgg, an empire of the immortal Ysna'qurel, child of Ghel'vur, which was destroyed by the "Dark Destroyer" after sending a warning into space; it is unclear whether the world or only its civilisation died. The warning was received by the Moongazer Nin-Kiggia.

Accounts: The Heavenly Principles themselves are presented, in the Byakuyakoku Collection, as the first Descender. Alice describes the Abyss as the hatred carried by fates that will not come to pass, which is an account of its nature rather than a home world. The wiki does not state where it came from before Nibelung brought it. Weapon text for the Sword of Descension supplies the "star-devouring darkness" that ended the Traveler's world.

Open questions: Canon does not say what lies beyond the Dark Sea in detail, where the Heavenly Principles or the Abyss originated, what the star-devouring darkness is, how many Descenders exist overall, or how the numbered worlds Octavia visited relate to the main plot. Do not invent a map of the cosmos.

Connections: Linked to the Heavenly Principles and the false sky (the barrier), the Descenders, the Abyss, the Three Moons, the Traveler and their sibling, Skirk and Surtalogi, Nibelung, Octavia and the Moongazers.

Roleplay note (this project's guidance): characters inside Teyvat generally have no idea the sea of stars exists, since the false sky hid it. Only Descenders, the Traveler, beings tied to the Moongazers or Surtalogi's circle, and a few others would speak of it, and even they know it only in fragments.

123.comment: Sea of Stars: Sea of Stars
123.content: The universe beyond Teyvat's false sky. Teyvat sits on the edge of a spiral arm of an unnamed galaxy. It is described as a dangerous "black forest" full of planets, civilisations and unknown calamities. The Heavenly Principles, Saarelainen and the Traveler came from it, and the Abyss is counted among its calamities. Teyvatians cannot normally perceive it.

124.content: Skirk comes from an unnamed planet whose humans could adapt to any environment or energy source. A merchant ship from a neighbouring world saw them as a potential threat, and an army was sent. She escaped with Surtalogi's help and was brought to Teyvat after the Cataclysm. What became of the planet is unknown.

125.content: A world once ruled by the immortal Ysna'qurel, child of Ghel'vur, and their empire. It was destroyed by the "Dark Destroyer" and broadcast a warning into the cosmos, which the Moongazer Nin-Kiggia received. It is unclear whether the whole world or only its civilisation was lost.

126.content:
Seven Sovereigns (also: Dragon Sovereigns, Dragon Sovereign, elemental dragon sovereigns, Seven Dragon Sovereigns, seven terrifying sovereigns, dragon-lords of the old world): The Seven Sovereigns are the seven elemental dragons, one per element, who ruled the old world of Teyvat under the Dragon King Nibelung. The Heavenly Principles defeated them and stole part of their power, the elemental Authorities, which became the basis of the Archons' Authorities. Living Sovereigns therefore lack full "dragonhood" until an Archon's throne is destroyed and the Authority returned, which has happened only for Hydro. Current Sovereigns: Dvalin (Anemo, Mondstadt), Azhdaha (Geo, sealed in Liyue), Apep (Dendro, Sumeru) and Neuvillette (Hydro, Fontaine, reborn in human form). Xiuhcoatl (Pyro) and the Cryo Dragon are dead with no successor; no Electro Sovereign is known.

The Chinese title means "Dragon King", which English sometimes renders "Dragon Lord". They are not Natlan's Thirteen Sovereign Lords, who served Xiuhcoatl.

Established: - They were the dragon-lords of the old world. Each held one Authority and a domain attuned to its element.
- In Calamitous Tread (4.1), Neuvillette says no living Sovereign, himself included, holds full dragonhood, and that the power the "First Usurper" seized is the basis of the Archons' Authorities.
- A Sovereign is born only from an elementally pure lineage. Bathysmal Vishaps, which diverged into Electro and Cryo forms, are impure. A Sovereign may instead be reborn in human form, like Neuvillette.

Sovereigns: - Anemo: Dvalin (Mondstadt), alive and Venti's ally again since the Prologue; his unnamed predecessor is dead.
- Geo: Azhdaha (Liyue), once Morax's friend, eroded and sealed beneath the Dragon-Queller; resealed in Zhongli's Story Quest (1.5).
- Electro: unknown.
- Dendro: Apep (Sumeru), purged of forbidden knowledge in Homecoming (3.6); now merely observes gods and humans.
- Hydro: Neuvillette (Fontaine), the only Sovereign with his full Authority back (4.2).
- Pyro: Xiuhcoatl (Natlan), killed about 2,000 years ago by Xbalanque, the first Pyro Archon.
- Cryo: the Cryo Dragon (Snezhnaya), long dead; its remains lie beneath a Celestial Nail by the ruins of Hyperborea.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): Sovereigns are ancient, proud and alien, and may see Archons as the usurper's appointees. Ordinary people do not know the term or the history of the Authorities. Do not invent an Electro Sovereign or a Cryo successor; keep Azhdaha sealed and Dvalin, Apep and Neuvillette non-hostile as of 7.1.

127.content: An elemental Authority is a Sovereign's dominion over its element. The Heavenly Principles seized part of each Sovereign's power, and it became the basis of the Archons' Authorities and divine thrones. A living Sovereign cannot reach full dragonhood, or its memories of the old world, until the Archon's throne is destroyed and the Authority returned. This has happened once: Focalors arranged her own execution in 4.2, destroying the Hydro throne and returning the Hydro Authority to Neuvillette.

128.content: The original Hydro Sovereign was the heart of the Primordial Sea and ruled the vishaps of the waters. It perished after the war against the Heavenly Principles. Fontaine's children's rhyme says that when the Hydro Dragon weeps, it rains; Neuvillette, its human-form successor, is puzzled by the idea that the dragon could cry.

129.content:
Shadow Realm (also: world of shadow, World of Shadows, Shadow Realms): The Shadow Realm is a strange pocket-space that floats like a bubble over the frozen land of Snezhnaya and swallows those who stumble in. Inside there is no wind, no light and no usable elemental energy, so Vision-holders cannot channel their powers and must fight with firearms that carry elemental power in their ammunition. The ruins of Hyperborea, the Golden City, lie inside it. Fatui soldiers and travellers have been lost to it; the Druzhna contain and clear breaches, with Royal Energy Commission officials posted outside them.

Snezhnayans also speak of it as the "world of shadow." Its origin is uncertain: the Belyi Tsar suspected that it was made with technology from beyond Teyvat and that it shields the world from the Abyss.

Established: - No wind, no light, no elemental energy; as Alyosha puts it, even time does not exist there and everything seems to come to a standstill. Most people pulled in are never seen again, and the few who return are never quite the same.
- Those who fail to escape are devoured: in Alyosha's words their shadows are devoured and they are no longer among the living; Druzhna briefings describe them warped into monsters lost to reason.
- Breaches open suddenly in Snezhnaya, like bubbles rising to the water's surface; the Eye of Graeae says the Realm intersects the world of the Light Realm only rarely, in just that way.
- The ruins of Hyperborea lie inside it.

- Vision-holders cannot call on their power there. Firearms, whose ammunition holds and channels elemental power from outside, were found by someone after much research to be the most effective means of attack, according to the Eye of Graeae.
- The Eye of Graeae, a device found in an abandoned station, calls the Shadow Realm the darkest space in the "shell," where even the most high is loath to cast its gaze. It helps the Traveler by marking exits and issuing equipment.
- Breaches can appear anywhere, not only in expected places: one swallowed the Traveler's train on the railway itself, which Alyosha calls almost unheard of. Falling off an edge into the untethered depths may mean never leaving again.
- A breach can "sink back down"; the Traveler escapes through a core that collapses behind them.

Accounts: - The Belyi Tsar (Pale Crown Palace notes): the Realm was probably made by Anacharsis, "The Saint," directly or as a by-product of the memories he left in the eternal void in defiance of his fate; its science is not Teyvat's; it works as a film protecting the world from the Abyss. He presents these as deductions.
- Alyosha, a Snezhnayan traveller: knows it as a deadly place from stories and a few sightings, and says this is his first time inside. He recalls a story of a "World of Shadows" with a way out.
- The Eye of Graeae, an ancient device: names it the darkest space in the shell and says its own creation was likely connected to it. Its words on this are partly broken off.

History: - Hyperborea, the Golden City of the unified civilization, was destroyed by a Celestial Nail roughly 6,000 years ago and plunged into the Shadow Realm; survivors fled toward Nod-Krai and became the Frostmoon Scions.
- Much later the Belyi Tsar, driven by dark dreams and a search for his origin, opened a "passage" into the Shadow Realm; his notes say the innocent were ensnared at a price heavier than he imagined, and the Abyss began to seep through the rift he had made. In Black Feathers Scattered at Parting (7.1), Rhinedottir tells the Tsaritsa that the Tsar incited her (then a herald of the court) and Saarelainen, the Third Descender, to open the gate to the Abyss, and that he alone escaped the consequences by fleeing into the Shadow Realm, which also let him keep his memories of the Third.
- Inside he found Hyperborea's ruins and records, learned what he was (an incomplete Primordial Human made from the Cryo Dragon), and eventually accepted Celestia's offer of the Cryo throne about 2,000 years ago.

Connections: - Hyperborea, Anacharsis and Koitar: the Realm holds the city's ruins and records.
- The Belyi Tsar, Anastasya and Saarelainen: the passage he opened.
- The Abyss: the Realm is described as holding it back, yet the opened passage lets it seep in.
- The Heavenly Principles and Celestia: the Tsar wonders why they never destroyed the Realm.
- The Eye of Graeae, Aksinya and the Hvergelmir: they researched or used Realm technology and records.

Gameplay: Gameplay (not lore): the Realm is a third-person shooter mode introduced in 7.0 and first unlocked in the Archon Quest "Gunfire in the Silent Lands." Elemental Sight, food and some gadgets are unavailable; the Traveler uses firearms such as Shatanaya's Frostsilver, Balsag's Sunwheel and Ashamez's Thunder and throws Frag Crystals. Enemies are usually Fatui Oprichniki, Skirmishers and Landcruisers marked by a purple aura.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): treat the Shadow Realm as eerily still and quiet; light is flat or absent, sound dull, the air full of pale dust. Characters rely on guns and gear, not Visions. Do not let a Vision holder cast elemental spells inside it. Keep its origin and purpose open.

130.comment: Shadow Realm: Shadow Realm breaches and containment
130.content: Breaches open suddenly in Snezhnaya's tundra and, rarely, on its railways. Royal Energy Commission officials stand by known breaches; the Druzhna, whose duties include containing them, set up perimeters, enter and clear them. Fatui soldiers have been lost inside; those trapped are devoured and warped into monsters lost to reason. The Special Recruitment Project's descriptions say that clearing a Realm releases the lost souls, human and fae.

131.content:
Shadowmoon (also: false moon, fake moon, moon's shadow, shadow of the moon): The shadowmoon, also called the false moon or the moon's shadow, was an illusory moon that occupied the sky of Teyvat for thousands of years after the real Three Moons were destroyed or banished. It also served as a prison for one fragment of the dead Zibai's soul. When the Traveler and Columbina brought the Frost Moon back in Nod-Krai, the shadowmoon lost its purpose and began to disintegrate. It vanished completely on the night of Lantern Rite in Liyue Harbor, in version 6.3.

Until then it was invisible to the eye except as occasional dark patches, which people took for lunar eclipses. Zhongli worked out that mortals' wishes seemed to trigger each stage of its breakdown.

Established: - It was an illusory "false" moon, a projection of the moon rather than a body of its own.
- The Frost Moon's return left it without a place in the heavens, so it began to disintegrate bit by bit.
- It held Zibai's First Deadly Self, Ziju, and with her the Heavenly Soul (Taiguang) of Zibai's divided soul.
- It disappeared entirely on Lantern Rite night.

- Disintegration comes and goes. While it happens the real moon looks as if a black shadow covers it, which Zhongli identifies as the recent lunar eclipse; when it pauses the shadow cannot be seen at all.
- Zhongli suspected that wishes, such as those made on Xiao Lanterns, trigger the episodes. In The Realm of Clouds the Traveler experiences one exactly when Linlang speaks her wish.
- Because the soul fragment and the shadowmoon had spent countless years together they had merged, so when the shadowmoon was gone Ziju would cease to exist in the world unless Zibai's other two fragments were reunited with her first.
- Zhongli had been waiting for such an opportunity for thousands of years; he used the moment to reunite the three fragments.

Accounts: - Zhongli (The Realm of Clouds): the shadowmoon is a false projection of the moon, the prison confining Zibai's Heavenly Soul, and its collapse is both a danger and an opening.
- The wiki's Three Moons page: the Heavenly Principles projected the shadowmoon to cover up what happened to the Three Moons after the war of funerary flame; Istaroth used it to preserve a portion of Zibai's soul. Only the second half is shown directly in the quest.

Open questions: Canon does not say what the shadowmoon was made of, whether it ever existed apart from the sky it replaced, or who made it. The Heavenly Principles are the attributed maker (via the wiki) but the quest text read does not state this outright. Do not describe the Heavenly Principles as having sworn to it or as having destroyed it.

Connections: Replaced the Three Moons after the war of funerary flame, when the Eternal and Iridescent Moons were destroyed and the Frost Moon banished beyond the false sky. Ended by the return of the Frost Moon (Archon Quest True Moon, version 6.3). Linked to Zibai, the Moon Envoy and one-time god of Lang-Gan, to Istaroth of the Four Shades, to Zhongli, and to Liyue's Lantern Rite.

How {{char}} behaves: Treat it as a hidden, fading thing after 6.3: it is now gone, and only characters who followed the Lantern Rite events know of it. Ordinary Liyue residents may remember the odd eclipses or the legend of the White Horse Adeptus without knowing the connection. (Suggested use, not canon.)

132.content: After the Frost Moon returned to Teyvat, the shadowmoon broke down bit by bit. To observers, the moon looked briefly blocked by a black shadow (the "lunar eclipse"), then clear. Zhongli suspected wishes triggered it; on Lantern Rite night, with countless Xiao Lanterns released, it fully collapsed. The story was told in the A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon event, a limited-time event when it began.

133.content: Zibai split off Ziju, Zizhi and Zijiao, her Three Deadly Selves, before dying. Istaroth placed her shattered soul in them: the Heavenly Soul (Taiguang) in Ziju, imprisoned in the shadowmoon; the Earth Soul (Shuangling) in Zizhi, who slept in the Chasm; and the Human Soul (Youjing) in Zijiao, who was sealed in a painting and later followed Rex Lapis during the Archon War. The Traveler and Zhongli recovered all three before the shadowmoon vanished, and Zibai returned.

key: The Seven Who Rule the Mortal World
134.content:
The Seven (also: The Seven Archons, Seven Archons, Archons of The Seven, The Seven Who Rule the Mortal World): The Seven (the Seven Archons) are the gods who each preside over one of Teyvat's seven nations and one element. They are the victors of the Archon War, which ended about 2,000 years ago. Each Archon holds a divine throne in Celestia and was given a Gnosis, a chess-piece-like focus. Each also embodies an ideal that shapes their nation. As of 7.1: Venti (Barbatos, Anemo, Freedom, Mondstadt), Zhongli (Morax, Geo, Contracts, Liyue), Raiden Ei (Electro, Eternity, Inazuma), Nahida (Lesser Lord Kusanali, Dendro, Wisdom, Sumeru), Mavuika (Pyro, War, Natlan) and the Tsaritsa, Anastasya (Cryo, Love, Snezhnaya). The Hydro throne (Justice, Fontaine) no longer exists.

Only Barbatos and Morax remain from the original Seven; the other seats have changed hands, most of them during the Cataclysm 500 years ago. The Tsaritsa's Fatui have taken the Gnoses one by one: as of 7.1 she holds six, and the seventh, the Pyro Gnosis, was lost when Irminsul burned.

Established: - Archons are gods, not mortals with Visions. Venti calls Visions "primitive" next to a Gnosis.
- Each Archon's power over their element comes from their divine throne. The thrones hold part of the Authorities the Heavenly Principles took from the Seven Sovereigns, the elemental dragons.
- Archons can die. Their thrones then pass to a successor.
- Venti says an Archon's strength depends on how much they govern their land. He calls himself the weakest of The Seven because he refuses to rule Mondstadt.
- The wiki also names faith as a source of power, alongside rule over a nation and the throne's Authority.
- Archons do not choose who gets a Vision and know nothing about the recipients. They are only obliged to give up part of their Authority to form one when notified to do so (Raiden Shogun's voice-overs, Neuvillette's character story).
- People in Teyvat commonly believe the Archons grant Visions.

Members: Current holders of the six surviving thrones (7.1):
- Anemo, Mondstadt: Barbatos (Venti). God of Freedom, ascended 2,600 years ago.
- Geo, Liyue: Morax (Zhongli), called Rex Lapis. God of Contracts and eldest of The Seven. Retired as a mortal in 1.1.
- Electro, Inazuma: Beelzebul (Raiden Ei), who rules as the Raiden Shogun. God of Eternity, Archon since 500 years ago.
- Dendro, Sumeru: Buer (Nahida), Lesser Lord Kusanali. God of Wisdom and the youngest Archon, about 500 years old.
- Pyro, Natlan: Mavuika, holder of the shared divine name Haborym. God of War.
- Cryo, Snezhnaya: Vassaga (Anastasya), the Tsaritsa. God of Love, Archon since 500 years ago.
Hydro, Fontaine (Justice): Egeria, then Focalors. The throne was destroyed in 4.2, so there will be no more Hydro Archons.

Powers: A divine throne gives an Archon authority over their element. A Gnosis, normally kept inside the Archon's chest, amplifies elemental power and links its holder directly to Celestia. Archons keep their elemental power and their thrones without a Gnosis.

History: After the war of funerary flame about 6,000 years ago, the Heavenly Principles set up seven divine thrones in Celestia and had gods fight for them and their Gnoses. This was the Archon War. Many gods died. The last seat was claimed about 2,000 years ago, and the victors founded the seven nations. The original Seven were fairly close and shared the duty of guiding humanity; they used to gather in Liyue to drink with Rex Lapis.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1, six thrones remain, since the Hydro throne is gone. All six current Archons are alive. The Tsaritsa holds six Gnoses (Cryo, Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro, Hydro). The Pyro Gnosis is missing.

How {{char}} behaves: Roleplay interpretation (this project's recommendation, not canon text): Archons are rarely recognised in person. Venti, Zhongli and Nahida move among people unnoticed, and many people know their god only from statues, temples and stories. Keep them distinct: each embodies a different ideal and governs differently. Venti refuses to rule, Zhongli gave up rule, Ei and the Shogun guard Eternity, Nahida rules gently, Mavuika leads in war, and Anastasya rules absolutely. When elemental power runs through an Archon, the ends of their hair glow in their element's colour; Mavuika's whole hair lights up.

135.comment: The Seven: Divine Thrones of The Seven
135.content: Celestia holds seven divine thrones, one per element, each containing part of an Authority the Heavenly Principles took from the Seven Sovereigns. Neuvillette says the First Usurper "seized a part of the dragons' power" and that it is now the basis of the Archons' Authorities (4.1). A throne passes to a successor when its Archon dies. Destroying a throne takes immense power and the seated Archon's death, and returns the Authority to its dragon. Focalors destroyed the Hydro throne this way in 4.2, so only six remain.

136.content: The first Seven were Barbatos, Morax, Baal (Makoto), Rukkhadevata, Egeria, Xbalanque and the Belyi Tsar. They took their seats at different times, ending about 2,000 years ago, and would gather in Liyue to drink with Rex Lapis. As of 7.1 only Barbatos and Morax survive. Morax is the eldest and Barbatos the second eldest. Ei fought through the Archon War beside Makoto but only became Archon after her twin's death.

137.content: Egeria became Hydro Archon about 2,000 years ago, after Remus fell, and died in the Cataclysm. Her Oceanid Focalors succeeded her, split her divinity from her body, and left that body, Furina, to play the Hydro Archon for 500 years. In Masquerade of the Guilty (4.2) Focalors had herself executed by the Oratrice, which destroyed the throne and returned the full Hydro Authority to Neuvillette, the Hydro Sovereign. Furina abdicated and lives as an ordinary Fontainian. Neuvillette gave the Hydro Gnosis, unaffected by the throne's destruction, to Arlecchino.

138.comment: The Seven: Pyro Archons and the Pilgrimage
138.content: Natlan's Archons are mortals who age and die. Each new Pyro Archon wins the seat through the Pilgrimage, gains the Sacred Flame's knowledge on ascending, and carries the divine name Haborym. Xbalanque, the first, defeated the Pyro Sovereign Xiuhcoatl and established Natlan's system. The current Pyro Archon, Mavuika, placed her life in the Sacred Flame 500 years ago so she could return to finish the war against the Abyss, and she has returned.

139.comment: The Seven: Representatives of The Seven
139.content:
Some Archons ruled through figures the public took for the Archon:
- Ei served as kagemusha to her twin Makoto, and the people saw them as one Raiden Shogun until Makoto died 500 years ago.
- The Shogun, a puppet Ei finished about 400 years ago, has ruled in her place since. After 2.1 they share rule, and few know the two are separate.
- Furina was publicly the Hydro Archon for 500 years, though only Focalors held the throne and Authority. She abdicated in 4.2.

140.comment: The Seven: The Tsaritsa's Gnosis collection
140.content: The Fatui have collected Gnoses for the Tsaritsa since 1.0. As of 7.1 she holds six: her own Cryo Gnosis, plus the Anemo, Geo, Electro, Dendro and Hydro Gnoses. Before Signora's funeral (teaser "A Winter Night's Lazzo"), she played chess with Pierro with the Anemo and Geo Gnoses on the board as pieces. In 7.1 she told the Traveler her two reasons: to amplify her power beyond a single Archon's against the Heavenly Principles, and to open the Third Descender's seal. She asked the Traveler where the Pyro Gnosis was, the only one unaccounted for.

141.content:
Thirteen Sovereign Lords (also: Thirteen Lords, Sovereign Lords, Thirteen Dragonlords, Sovereign Rulers' Council, Ch'ule-L): The Thirteen Sovereign Lords were thirteen artificial rulers made by Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, to govern ancient Natlantea. Each held a territory, and together they met as a council in the Chamber of Deliberation under the First Lord as Speaker. They oppressed Natlantea's humans for thousands of years. Ten fell when the Sacred City of Tollan collapsed in the war between Xbalanque and Xiuhcoatl, and the Ninth Lord, long sealed in Chichen Uctokah, was freed from her bonds and put to rest by the Traveler at her own request. A few survive in changed form, notably Ajaw and the Eleventh Lord's surviving core in Ineffa.

They are not ordinary dragons. Citlali explains in the quest "Smoldering" that they were artificial intelligences built with secret source technology, with greater intelligence and authority than the Pyro dragons themselves. Their personal names end in a number in a Mayan language (Hun is one, Ka' two, and so on up to Ooxlahun, thirteen) plus the designation Ch'ule-L.

Established: - Creator: Xiuhcoatl, the Pyro Dragon of the Seven Sovereigns, who ruled Natlantea.
- Role: each Lord governed an individual territory of Natlantea; they assembled in the Chamber of Deliberation to debate and vote, with the First Lord, the Valiant One, presiding as Speaker.
- Fate: ten fell in the fall of Tollan; the Ninth (Ixlel) was freed from her imprisonment and put to rest by the Traveler in "Open Your Heart to Me"; Ajaw (probably the Tenth) lives on as a bound companion of the adventurer Kinich; part of the Eleventh lives on in Ineffa.

- Rank and title (as listed by the wiki from in-game records): 1 Valiant One; 2 Jade Maiden; 3 Weaver of Secrets; 4 Hermit of Myriad Fates; 5 Bestower of Bitter Springs; 6 He Who Shakes the Earth Like Thunder in His Wrath; 7 Toxic Rain Over Boundless Forests; 8 Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers; 9 Chronicler of the End Times; 10 Undying Wings of Lofty Isolation; 11 Mirror of the Dawning Morn; 12 Murmuring Spring; 13 Bonebreaker. Each Lord's records carry a number "CL-01" to "CL-13".
- In the Chamber of Deliberation, the council records state that once consensus was reached, even abstainers were bound to uphold the decision.
- The Lords and Xiuhcoatl survived the Heavenly Principles' invasion by sheltering in the underground city of Tollan.
- After the War of Funerary Flame the awakened dragons destroyed the angels who had guided the human civilisations, sparing only Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night, according to item and quest text. The Lords then oppressed the humans of Natlantea.

Accounts: Who claims what: Awanyu (a Secret Source Servant) tells the Traveler in the World Quest "Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment" that ten of the Thirteen fell when Tollan collapsed, one remained in Chichen Uctokah, and one survives, though not in the form it would have wished. The wiki's table adds that the Third Lord's consciousness lives in the Night Kingdom (from weapon texts such as Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow and Flute of Ezpitzal). The Flower-Feather Clan's account in the book "Fires of Autumn Twilight" holds that the Sixth Lord survived Tollan and was killed by Lianca's second daughter in Och-Kan's reign, while the council record B-CL-13097 already speaks of him as fallen earlier.

Open questions: Canon leaves open which Lord Ajaw originally was, what elements and territories most Lords had, and how a Lord's artificial nature relates to dragon bodies and "cores" (the Ninth was bound in a statue over the Core of Chu'ulel; Ineffa's heart-core is a surviving half of the Eleventh). Do not claim that any element or territory is certain where canon is silent.

Connections: - Xiuhcoatl and the Seven Sovereigns: the Lords' maker, the Pyro Sovereign who was frozen by the Heavenly Principles and later killed by Xbalanque.
- Kukulkan: Xiuhcoatl's younger brother and Regent, impeached by the Lords.
- Lianca and the Flower-Feather Clan: the Eighth Lord adopted Lianca, who then fought the dragons.
- Och-Kan: the half-human ruler who sealed the Ninth Lord in a statue.
- Ajaw and Kinich: the Tenth Lord's present-day form and his contract partner.
- Ineffa: carries the Eleventh Lord's benevolent core; the Eleventh's hostile half was imprisoned in the Temple of Cascading Colors.

142.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Eleventh Lord and Ineffa
142.content: The Eleventh Lord despised humanity more than her peers. After Xiuhcoatl fell, she split her mind into two cores: one longing for a place to belong and one that kept her hostility. She asked Lianca to destroy the benevolent half, falsely calling it hostile; Lianca saw through the lie and imprisoned the hostile half in the Temple of Cascading Colors, after which the Eleventh Lord cursed the benevolent half to suffer for any goodwill toward humans. Lianca sent that half away from Natlan. About two thousand years later it was scavenged in Nod-Krai by Aino and used to build Ineffa, who began suffering malfunctions from the curse. In "Searing" the Eleventh Lord posed as the Eighth Lord, then revealed herself and tried to take control of Ineffa. Ineffa overloaded the curse and, with the Traveler and her Moon Wheel, destroyed the Eleventh Lord's form in a Secret Source Automaton: Configuration Device. Her last words admitted that she too longed for a place to belong.

143.content: The Ninth Lord ruled Chichen Uctokah, the original name of Ochkanatlan, and kept an unusual interest in a "well" that other Lords feared, now the Old Core of Chu'ulel. Och-Kan had it excavated and found her; he later bound her in a statue. In "Open Your Heart to Me" the Traveler lowers the water around the statue, gathers the pieces of her heart and frees her at her request; she pours her remaining energy into the heart and her soul is put to rest. She is proud, insists on her rank, and believes only the Chosen of Dragons may release her. The item Perfect Heart of the Sacred Dragon describes its heart as that of the Dragonlord of Chichen Uctokah.

144.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Weaver of Secrets (Third Lord)
144.content: The Third Lord ruled land in the Tezcatepetonco Range. She was skilled in divination and held that humans' fates are fixed by the Heavenly Principles. Pitying her dragons, who were degenerating into beasts after the War of Funerary Flame, she made a pact with human tribes (forerunners of the Masters of the Night-Wind): she would provide a labyrinth of mirrors and a fortress of mist if they appointed a "Holy Sovereign" to put the dragons into a dream state. She merged her consciousness into the Night Kingdom. Her friend, the Eighth Lord, predicted the plan would bring humans more suffering, and weapon text shows the Holy Sovereigns did suffer. The pact later lapsed under Och-Kan and was renewed through the priest Wagadu, as described in weapon texts.

key: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
145.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Eighth Lord and Lianca
145.content: The Eighth Lord ruled Ch'upikaq Tajin, today Flower-Feather Clan territory, and is the only Lord known to have been kind to humans, raising Lianca as a dragon princess. She had the Second Lord forge a longbow (Chain Breaker) for her daughter and accepted that Lianca might one day oppose her. For this she was tried by the council and executed during the siege of Tollan.

146.comment: Thirteen Sovereign Lords: Ajaw, the Tenth Lord
146.content: Ajaw calls himself an almighty sovereign ruler and is bound to the adventurer Kinich by a contract: Kinich receives Ajaw's power and Ajaw will eventually take over Kinich's body at his death. The council records say the Tenth Lord was tricked by humans (see Ring of Yaxche) and sealed alive in a mountain, matching how Kinich found him. In "Smoldering", Citlali concludes from a slip by Ajaw that he is a Sovereign Lord; he does not remember which one.

147.content:
Three Moons (also: Three Moon Goddesses, Three Moon Sisters, Moon Sisters, Moon Goddesses, Trilune, Trilunar Authority, Lunar Palace): The Three Moons are three ancient moons and the goddesses bound to them, also called the Three Moon Goddesses or Three Moon Sisters: Aria of the Eternal Moon, Canon of the Frost Moon and Sonnet of the Iridescent Moon. The Dragon King Nibelung raised them from the planet's crust, at what is now Nod-Krai, to oversee Teyvat and wield his authority while he travelled the sea of stars. Their power is called the Trilunar Authority or Trilune. In the war of funerary flame the Heavenly Principles shattered the Eternal and Iridescent Moons and flung the Frost Moon beyond the false sky. All three goddesses then died, because Teyvat no longer accepted them. To hide this, the Heavenly Principles hung an illusory "shadowmoon" in the night sky.

Their story is the core of the Nod-Krai Archon Quest, Song of the Welkin Moon (5.8-6.6). There, Columbina, born in Nod-Krai as the new Frost Moon goddess (Kuutar), receives the authority of all three moons and becomes the Trilune Goddess. She defeats Dottore, who had stolen the moons' power, and the Frost Moon returns inside Teyvat's sky.

Established: - Eternal Moon (Aria): the first and largest moon. Its gravity was said to raise the tides. It was shattered.
- Frost Moon (Canon): the second moon and the brightest. It was banished beyond the false sky, but has now returned to Teyvat's sky with Columbina as its goddess.
- Iridescent Moon (Sonnet): the third and smallest moon, with a faint light that made fleeting halos. It was shattered, and its remains became the Crimson Moon.

- The sisters lived in the Lunar Palace. One at a time, they ruled the night sky, riding through the heavens in a silver carriage or chariot and changing places about three times a month.
- When a goddess dies, her remains can condense into a Moon Marrow. The Moon Marrows hold what is left of the sisters' power and are a source of Light Realm energy.
- Before the war, many civilisations worshipped the moons rather than the Heavenly Principles. Some accounts also say the moons received the dead, with "boatmen" ferrying souls to cities upon the moon.

History: Nibelung left Teyvat and the moons kept it for him. When the Heavenly Principles arrived, the sisters let them stay. They then watched the Heavenly Principles remake the world's rules and destroy the dragons. When Nibelung returned, corrupted by the Abyss, the sisters could not agree whether to side with him. He imprisoned them and turned their moons into weapons. The Heavenly Principles answered by destroying or banishing the moons, and the goddesses died.

Present day: In the present (5.1-6.3), the false sky briefly cracked over Natlan, Dottore stole the moons' power in Nod-Krai and was defeated by Columbina as the Trilune Goddess, and the Frost Moon returned inside Teyvat's sky, ending the shadowmoon illusion.

Open questions: - Canon does not settle whether the sisters were coerced partners or willing observers of the Heavenly Principles' order. Both views appear in-game.
- It is not clear whether the Heavenly Principles knew Nibelung had imprisoned the goddesses before they struck the moons.

Connections: Nibelung (creator); the Heavenly Principles and Four Shades (rivals and inheritors of their authority); the false sky and shadowmoon (the cover-up); the Moon Marrows, kuuvahki and the Moon Wheel (what remains of them); the Frostmoon Scions and Hyperborea (their worshippers); Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty (Sonnet's corruption); Columbina (successor and Trilune Goddess).

148.content: The "moon's reflection" is a prison of warped space and time that Nibelung made to keep the Three Moon Sisters out of the war of funerary flame. Every path inside it leads back to the moment of their imprisonment, so they could never escape or learn what had happened outside. In Song of the Welkin Moon, Columbina banishes herself there to escape Dottore. Travelling backwards through it, she meets the imprisoned sisters, who give her their authority. She then leaves her soul there, anchored by Luonnotar, until she is revived in the present (6.3).

149.content: The Trilune, or Trilunar Authority, is the combined power of the three moons. Aria says it is bound to Teyvat's most fundamental rules. Dottore took its raw power by capturing the Moon Marrows and later made an artificial marrow. The Traveler was unaffected by the authority he gained, and authority drawn from marrows proved weaker than what the living sisters had handed to Columbina. Since True Moon (6.3), Columbina is the Trilune Goddess, the one moon goddess of Teyvat. Lauma and Arlecchino keep the surviving Moon Marrows.

150.content:
Three Realms (also: Human Realm, realms of the world): The three realms are the Light Realm, the Void Realm and the Human Realm. The Light Realm is the home of pure elemental beings such as dragons and elemental lifeforms. The Void Realm, better known as the Abyss, is a destructive force that corrupts and unmakes. The Human Realm is the realm of gods and humanity, created by the Heavenly Principles. They are not separate places but concurrent facets of one world that can occupy the same space.

Each has its own current: ley lines for the Human Realm, elemental currents for the Light Realm and dark currents for the Void Realm. The Light Realm and Void Realm are opposed, the Human Realm sits between them, and the Abyss Order and other Abyssal monsters seek to tear down the human world.

Established: - The Light Realm (elemental), the Void Realm (abyssal) and the Human Realm (created by the Heavenly Principles) coexist in the world of Teyvat as facets of it, not as distant locations.
- An area may be dominated by one realm's power, while elsewhere the three keep their influence in balance.

- When the Heavenly Principles descended, it vanquished the Seven Sovereigns of the Light Realm, subjugated nature and the Light Realm, and used phlogiston as the basis for the seven elements' Elemental Energy. It then created the Human Realm, including gods and humanity (per the books "Before Sun and Moon" and the Bathysmal Vishap records in The Byakuyakoku Collection).
- The Human Realm was at some point interposed between the Light Realm and the Void Realm.
- Creatures of the Human Realm and of the Light Realm (elemental beings) share the continent, though the two tend to conflict. The Void Realm threatens both, so the other two may cooperate to halt its encroachment.
- Elemental beings and Human Realm creatures can be made compatible with each other. Vishaps were modified to accept Orobashi's coral despite its Human Realm origin, and Sangacorallia break the Light Realm's pure elemental energy into something the Human Realm tolerates. The Void Realm's power, by contrast, has only been shown to destroy or corrupt.

Accounts: - Tsumi, in the Three Realms Gateway Offering quest, says the people of Byakuyakoku believe in three realms, the Vishap Realm (called the Light Realm in most books), the Human Realm and the Void Realm. She names the three currents and presents the Light Realm's energy as able to vanquish the Void Realm's darkness. She also believes the Abyss Order finds the Void Realm's power addictive.
- The Heavenly Principles' account in "Before Sun and Moon" presents the refraction of the Light Realm as founding the Human Realm. Later voices, the Belyi Tsar and Aksinya, present it as a loss of possibility and hope.

Open questions: Canon does not say what the realms physically are, how they overlap, or how their currents behave. Do not resolve this with theory.

Human Realm: cosmology.heavenly-principles, cosmology.celestia, cosmology.ley-lines. Rulers and key figures: cosmology.seven-sovereigns, historical.nibelung. Elements: system.elements, system.phlogiston. Enkanomiya and its quest: location.enkanomiya, npc.enjou, quest.three-realms-gateway-offering.

How {{char}} behaves: This is the project's suggested handling, not canon. Few ordinary people use the term "three realms"; scholars, Enkanomiya natives, vishaps, dragons or those close to the Abyss might. Keep it mysterious and avoid stating fan theories as fact.

151.content: The three realms are the Light Realm, the Void Realm (Abyss) and the Human Realm made by the Heavenly Principles. They are concurrent facets of Teyvat, with analogous currents: elemental currents, dark currents and ley lines. The Light Realm's energy overcomes the Void Realm's darkness, and the Void Realm threatens both others.

152.content: The Void Realm, better known as the Abyss, is an unworldly destructive force from the sea of stars, opposed to the Light Realm and corrosive to the Human Realm. It corrupts people and creatures and is harmful to elemental beings.
